attorneys.practice_type: Personal Injury Lawyers in Phoenix, AZ
attorneys.bio:
Nasser Abujbarah is an attorney in the personal injury division at Phillips Law Group, P.C. Nasser’s family immigrated from the Middle East in 1988 and landed in Phoenix, Arizona and he has lived here ever since. He received his undergraduate degree from Arizona State University, graduating summa cum laude with a degree in Finance. With a deep desire to stay in the state he loves, Nasser then went to law school at the Sandra Day O’Connor School of Law at Arizona State University, once again graduating with honors. During law school, Nasser received numerous scholastic awards and honors and when it was recently time to take the Arizona Bar Exam, he achieved the third highest score in the state.

Nasser’s sole focus at Phillips Law Group is to seek justice for those who have been aggrieved by the negligence of others. He is licensed in Arizona. He has represented many clients with different types of claims including motor vehicle accidents, premises liability and wrongful death.

attorneys.name: Marc Adair
attorneys.practice_type: Criminal Lawyers in Mesa, AZ
attorneys.bio: With more than 30 years of dedicated legal service, Marc Adair has solidified his reputation as a cornerstone of the Arizona legal community. Currently serving as a Senior Criminal Defense Attorney at Grand Canyon Law Group, Marc is far more than just a legal practitioner; he is a fierce advocate who brings a seasoned, aggressive edge to every case he handles. His career is fueled by a genuine, singular passion for criminal justice and a deep-seated belief in protecting the constitutional rights of every individual who finds themselves facing the power of the state. Marc’s journey to his current role was built on a long-standing foundation of leadership and professional independence. Before joining his current team, he spent over 25 years successfully navigating the complexities of the legal world as both a partner in a firm and as a sole practitioner. He further sharpened his high-stakes litigation expertise. This diverse history—which includes valuable experience as a former business owner—gives him a unique, well-rounded perspective that makes him an asset not just in the courtroom, but as a mentor and supervisor within any legal organization. In his practice today, Marc is the advocate people turn to when the stakes are at their highest. He is primarily tasked with defending clients through some of the most daunting legal challenges imaginable, including homicide, kidnapping, aggravated assault, and complex sex or drug offenses involving wiretaps. Whether he is appearing in an Arizona state court or a Federal U.S. District Court, Marc utilizes his strong interpersonal and communication skills to help the criminally accused navigate a system that often feels overwhelming and cold. For Marc, the practice of law is a true calling, centered on the idea that every person deserves a perfect advocate to fight for their rights.

attorneys.name: John P. Ager
attorneys.practice_type: Medical Malpractice Lawyers in Phoenix, AZ
attorneys.bio:
I am a life-long Arizona resident. I earned my undergraduate degree from the University of California, Berkeley, where I double majored in rhetoric and social science with an emphasis in legal theory. I earned my law degree from the University of Arizona College of Law the where I was a member of the Law Review and served as an extern to U.S. District Court Judge Hon. Richard Bilby. Since then, I have trained at trial colleges hosted by the National Institute for Trial Advocacy and the State Bar of Arizona. I also completed the program Mediating the Litigated Case at the world renowned Pepperdine Law School Straus Institute for Dispute Resolution.

I have been litigating personal injury and wrongful death cases, specializing in medical malpractice cases, for over 25 years. I am a board-certified specialist in personal injury and wrongful death litigation. I have successfully tried many cases to verdict. I am a Fellow of the American College of Trial Lawyers and a member of the American Board of Trial Advocates, both leading, peer-reviewed invitation-only associations of experienced trial lawyers and judges. I am rated AV-Preeminent by Martindale-Hubbell, indicating my peers rank me at the highest level of ethical and professional excellence. Since 2016, I have been recognized annually by Best Lawyers in America for my work in personal injury cases, most recently as Lawyer of the Year for both 2022 and 2024. Since 2015, I have been recognized annually by Southwest Super Lawyers for my work in medical malpractice cases. In eight years as chair of the State Bar of Arizona College of Trial Advocacy, I substantially redeveloped the curriculum of the Bar’s premiere trial lawyer development program. Since 2007, I have served on the State Bar of Arizona Civil Practice and Procedure Committee, the Bar’s leading committee responsible for drafting and reviewing the rules governing the way civil cases are litigated.

In his free time, Bonaventure enjoys playing soccer and is an avid fan of the Washington Commanders and Chelsea Football Club.

attorneys.name: Michael Alarid III
attorneys.firm_name: The Law Office of Michael Alarid III
attorneys.practice_type: Criminal Defense Lawyers in Phoenix, AZ
attorneys.bio:
Michael Alarid, III is a preeminent criminal defense attorney in the State of Arizona. His passion for criminal defense started when he was a young child listening to his father's stories about representing his criminal clients in New Mexico. After graduating the University of New Mexico, Mr. Alarid moved to Arizona to attend law school at Arizona State University. While in law school Mr. Alarid won his first felony jury trial in the public defender clinic where he appeared in court as a Rule 38 certified student attorney. At law school graduation, Mr. Alarid received the award for Distinguished Achievement in the Art and Science of Advocacy from The International Academy of Trial Lawyers.

After graduating from law school at ASU, Mr. Alarid went to work for one of the most distinguished boutique criminal defense firms in Arizona. During that time Mr. Alarid cut his teeth handling complex high-profile cases, including arguing before the Arizona Supreme Court twice within the first five years of his career-an opportunity most lawyers never experience in an entire career. In one of those cases, Mr. Alarid successfully persuaded the Arizona Supreme Court to change the law on marijuana DUIs statewide.

After five years at the boutique law firm, Mr. Alarid joined one of the largest criminal defense firms in Arizona. During his seven years as a trial attorney at the firm, Mr. Alarid continued to handle complex high-profile cases. Mr. Alarid gained invaluable experience handling hundreds of criminal cases of all types, taking dozens of cases, both misdemeanor and felony, to verdict at a jury trial. Mr. Alarid handles every aspect of criminal defense including pre-charge investigations, discovery review, witness interviews, pretrial motions, plea negotiations, professional board investigations and hearings, evidentiary hearings of all types, bench trials, jury trials, and state and federal appeals. He has handled every type of misdemeanor and felony criminal case including traffic offenses, DUI, theft, assault, domestic violence, drug cases, gun cases, vehicular crimes, sex crimes, white collar crimes, and homicides. Mr. Alarid has practiced in courts all across the state of Arizona including city courts, county courts, superior courts, the lower court of appeals, the Arizona Court of Appeals, the Arizona Supreme Court, and U.S. District Court of Arizona.

Mr. Alarid is Board Certified in DUI Defense Law by the National College for DUI Defense (NCDD), the only DUI board certification recognized by the American Bar Association. He is 1 of only 5 attorneys in the State of Arizona who have passed the NCDD Board Certification Examination. He was also selected to National Trial Lawyers Top 40 under 40 for 2020. Mr. Alarid is a member of the National Association of Criminal Defense Lawyers (NACDL) and the Arizona Attorneys for Criminal Justice (AACJ).

attorneys.name: Javier Alatorre
attorneys.practice_type: Civil Litigation Lawyers in Tucson, AZ
attorneys.bio:
Javier Alatorre is an attorney concentrating his practice in the areas of civil litigation, criminal defense & prosecution, real estate, municipal and government matters, as well as legal consulting in Mexican legal affairs. Mr. Alatorre holds several law degrees: a "Licenciatura en Derecho" or Bachelor of law degree from Universidad Panamericana in Mexico City, an LLM or Master of Laws degree, and JD or Jurisdoctor degree, from the William S. Richardson School of Law of the University of Hawaii. Javier has significant practical experience of over 10 years, and an exemplary dedication to the legal profession.

Before joining our firm in 2009, Javier worked at the Pima County Public Defender's office; a Hawaii based law firm; he was a teaching/research assistant for the William S. Richardson School of Law, of the University of Hawaii; and he also worked as a clerk with the United States District Court for the District of Hawaii, under the Honorable J. Michael Seabright. While in law school Javier worked with the Hawaii Innocence Project, and continues to do so as a volunteer attorney, liaising between Hawaii and Hawaiian inmates currently in custody in prisons located in Arizona, and contributing to post-conviction proceedings for these inmates.

Javier is a native of Hermosillo, Sonora, Mexico. He obtained his first law degree from "Universidad Panamericana" in Mexico City, and continued to live and work there until 2005, when he enrolled in the William S. Richardson School of Law of the University of Hawaii. When he is away from the office he enjoys swimming, and scuba diving, as well as visiting his home town of Hermosillo.

attorneys.name: Donald R. Alvarez
attorneys.practice_type: Real Estate Transactions Lawyers in Scottsdale, AZ
attorneys.bio:
Don Alvarez practices primarily in civil litigation, including business and commercial litigation, and plaintiff's personal injury and wrongful death. He also has extensive experience in litigating construction-related disputes for owners, general contractors, subcontractors and material suppliers.

Don is an "AV" rated attorney in Martindale-Hubbell's listings of attorneys. He is a member of the State Bar of Arizona, the New York State Bar Association, the American Bar Association, the Maricopa County Bar Association, the Association of Trial Lawyers of America, the Arizona Association for Justice (fka Arizona Trial Lawyers Association), the Scottsdale Bar Association, and Arizona's Finest Lawyers (Sustaining Member). He is admitted to practice in the District Courts of New York (Northern and Southern Districts), and Arizona, and the Ninth Circuit Court of Appeals. He has also been admitted to practice in the District Court of North Dakota. He is also a member of the American Arbitration Association, having served on its panel of arbitrators since 1980. Don has served on the Board of Trustees of the Maricopa County Bar Foundation (Chairman 2005) and the city of Scottsdale's Judicial Appointments Advisory Board.

Don was born and raised in Niagara Falls, New York. He earned a B.A. in history from Allegheny College in Meadville, Pennsylvania. He received his Juris Doctor degree from Albany Law School in Albany, New York in 1975. Immediately following his admission to the New York State Bar, he entered private practice. In 1979, he relocated to Arizona and was admitted to practice here in 1980.

Don has always been actively involved in the community. He has served on the Board of Directors of Youth Partners Foundation, Canyon State Academy and Arizona Boys Ranch, and has served as a Foundation Board Trustee for The Boys and Girls Club of Metropolitan Phoenix. He also has been a member of the Phoenix Sundown Rotary, serving as Secretary, Treasurer and President.

Kathy has experience in tax law, family law, real estate law, personal injury, probate, and estate planning. She also has a background in real estate investments, business management, and small business strategy.

In her free time, Kathy enjoys spending time with her two sons and grandson. She also enjoys traveling, golf, snowboarding, live music and dancing, biking, camping, and is a fan of anything involving the outdoors and staying active.

attorneys.name: William M. Bache
attorneys.practice_type: Personal Injury -- Plaintiff Lawyers in Oro Valley, AZ
attorneys.bio:
Bill Bache and his law partner, Frances Lynch, work as team to obtain justice for victims of serious personal injury and wrongful death. In recent years they have recovered substantial compensation for the families of people killed in motor vehicle accidents caused by: negligent road design and maintenance, drunk driving, and the over-serving of alcoholic beverages by a bar. They have helped numerous people regain their lives after suffering devastating injuries, including injuries to the brain, the spine, and amputation. They have recovered millions of dollars for their clients. To achieve this record of success, they combine hard work with over 40 years of personal injury experience. They thoroughly investigate each case and employ expert witnesses as necessary to get the proof they need. They have a passion for their clients and they work tirelessly for them, leaving no stone unturned in seeking full compensation for their losses.

Bill began his legal career working for one of the best law firms in Indiana after graduating near the top of his law school class at Indiana University. That law firm defended insurance companies and corporations in personal injury and wrongful death lawsuits. There, Bill learned about the insurance industry, and the tactics used by insurance companies and their lawyers to defeat claims for compensation by injury victims. Thereafter, Bill left to start his own firm, which would represent people, not insurance companies. He wanted to use what he had learned about the insurance industry and its tactics, to help injury victims and their families obtain justice. He has now been on the side of injury victims for over 30 years. He has lived and practiced law in Tucson since 1991.

Having grown up on farms in Pennsylvania and Indiana, I developed a strong work ethic early on. I also learned and believe in the principles of responsibility and accountability, and the Golden Rule - treat others how you wish to be treated. These principles govern my practice of law. Put simply, I care about our clients and do everything I can to help them through the process and to recover physically, emotionally, and financially.

When a person or company causes an injury to an innocent victim, the person or company must be held accountable, not only so that the injured person can be compensated for the total damages sustained, but also so that the person or company causing the injury will learn and take precautions to prevent future accidents or injury. Such prevention is paramount to keeping all of us safe.

Insurance companies, however, typically take any and all actions possible to avoid paying compensation to the injured. Often, they refuse to accept responsibility, and in many cases blame the injured for the cause of an accident.

I know how insurance companies use these tactics--I used to represent them.

As a former attorney for insurance companies, I also know what it takes to get cases settled. Because it is in their financial best interest to avoid paying out damages, reasonable settlements are almost never offered until a case is proven. The standard for proof usually goes beyond what is required at trial; in order to make a reasonable settlement offer, it usually must be clear to the insurance company that they will lose at least the amount of the settlement offer, and possibly much more, at trial.

Getting insurance companies to accept this realization requires hard work and dedication. We often need to interview witnesses, examine accident scenes, take depositions of experts, meet with doctors and other care providers so that we can prove the insurance company is liable for the damages sustained. While this work is tedious and time-consuming, it's the only way that fair compensation can be gained, either through a settlement or at trial.

attorneys.practice_type: Real Estate Lawyers in Goodyear, AZ
attorneys.bio:
D. Alexander Baker, a seasoned attorney based in Phoenix, Arizona, offers a wealth of proficiency in real estate and commercial law. Practicing at Faith Law, he adeptly handles a broad spectrum of legal issues, ranging from commercial transactions and lease negotiations to litigation concerning both residential and commercial real estate. His legal acumen extends to handling financing documentation, entity formation, construction disputes and property tax-related matters.

A consummate professional, he has spent over a decade honing his skills at various prestigious law firms, bringing a deep understanding of the local legal landscape to his clients. Mr. Baker's legal journey commenced at Arizona State University (ASU) where he earned his Juris Doctor degree, graduating with cum laude honors. His academic prowess was further demonstrated earlier at the W. P. Carey School of Business at ASU, where he achieved a Bachelor of Science degree in business management, graduating summa cum laude.

This solid educational foundation has equipped him with a robust understanding of the intricacies of business management, which complements his legal practice. Clients and fellow attorneys commend Mr. Baker for his detailed approach and dedication to delivering superior service. His ability to achieve favorable outcomes, whether through astute negotiations or in court, is highly valued. Testimonials often highlight his integrity, thoroughness and the personalized attention he provides to each case, ensuring that client needs are met with the utmost professionalism and care.

Mr. Baker's professional affiliations are a testament to his standing in the legal community. His roles and contributions to various legal associations underscore his commitment to legal excellence. At Faith Law, he continues to contribute to the firm's legacy of quality legal solutions and client-centered service, upholding its mission to address client needs effectively and foster lasting relationships.

Roie M. Bar is a partner and co-founder of Bar Urness, PLC. Mr. Bar earned his J.D. from the Sandra Day O’Connor School of Law, in conjunction with his M.B.A. from the W.P. Carey School of Business at Arizona State University. He received his undergraduate degree from Indiana University, where he was an Accounting and Finance major, and worked in the accounting field before going to law school.

Prior to starting his practice at Bar Urness, Mr. Bar practiced commercial litigation with the law firm of Wilenchik & Bartness, P.C., where he handled construction litigation cases, contractual disputes, and a variety of other business-related litigation cases. Mr. Bar’s current practice is primarily focused in the areas of Commercial Litigation, Real Estate Law, Estate Planning, and Business Transactions. His cases vary from Business Formations to Dissolutions; Contractual Disputes; Franchising Disputes; Insurance Litigation; Construction Litigation; Landlord-Tenant Relations; Property-Tax Appeals; HOA Disputes; Drafting Wills and Trusts; and Collections.

attorneys.bio:
Attorney Jason Barrat focuses his practice on wage and hour employment law. Mr. Barrat helps victims who are not compensated their full minimum wages or overtime wages. attorneys.name: Richard L. Barrett
attorneys.practice_type: Plaintiff's Personal Injury Lawyers in Phoenix, AZ
attorneys.bio:
Richard Barrett started working in private practice in 1978 and throughout the course of his law career, has focused on providing legal representation for individuals who were wrongfully harmed as a result of others' negligence or misconduct. He has experience representing individuals who have been injured by unsafe premises and products on premises as well as dangerous conditions at businesses and residences which cause individuals to slip and fall or trip and fall. He has significant experience in the transportation industry representing clients in matters involving injuries caused by the operation of or condition of automobiles, airplanes and trains. He works hard to secure settlements for his clients from insurance companies, major corporations, government entities, and others that caused his clients harm. He has performed mediation, arbitration, jury trials, and appeals across federal, tribal, and state courts.

Richard is admitted to practice in all Arizona state courts, the United States District Court for Arizona, and the 9th Circuit of the United States Court of Appeals.

attorneys.practice_type: Lawyers in Phoenix, AZ
attorneys.bio:
JOHN H. BARRON, III is a member of Barron & Polk, PLLC, Of Counsel to DeConcini McDonald Yetwin & Lacy, PC in the Phoenix and Flagstaff offices. John received his B.A. and J.D. degrees from the University of Arizona, and is admitted to the State Bar of Arizona and the United States District Court for the District of Arizona, as well as the State Bar of Georgia. John has served as co-chair and secretary for the Mental Health and Elder Law Section of the State Bar of Arizona. He is an associate editor of the 2000 Probate Code Practice Manual (4th ed.).

While practicing in Tucson, Mr. Barron was a special deputy Pima County attorney handling mental health litigation for Pima, Pinal, Yuma, and La Paz counties. Subsequently, Mr. Barron served as a deputy Maricopa County attorney representing the Maricopa County Medical Center Psychiatric Annex with respect to civil commitments and, later, representing the Maricopa County Public Fiduciary in the administration and litigation of estate, guardianship, conservatorship and mental health matters.

Subsequent to his return to private practice in 1997, Mr. Barron has established himself as a litigator of matters relating to estates, trusts, guardianships, conservatorships, exploitation and/or abuse of vulnerable or incapacitated adults, and eligibility of continued services for persons entitled to mental health and developmental disability related assistance.

In addition to the specific practice of law, Mr. Barron has also been a presenter and keynote speaker at seminars related to probate and mental health law, in-service training programs related to probate, guardianship and mental health law for medical personnel, and was the Instructor for the Arizona Supreme Court Fiduciary Training Program, Decision Marking module.

attorneys.name: Jawana Baxter
attorneys.practice_type: Lawyers in Mesa, AZ
attorneys.bio:
Jawana S. Baxter is an Associate Attorney who works with individuals accused of crimes, guiding them through the process and standing by them every step of the way. She focuses on making sure the state meets its burden and helps clients understand what is happening so they can feel more informed and prepared.

She is known for being organized, well prepared, and direct in her communication. Clients appreciate that she is honest and clear, especially when challenges come up. She works closely with clients and paralegals, and she puts effort into building professional relationships that help move cases forward. In addition, her calm and problem-solving approach helps people feel more at ease.

Before joining the firm, Jawana spent 10 years as a lead litigation paralegal at a personal injury firm. She later attended Arizona State University, where she earned her law degree and a trial advocacy certificate, building on her strong foundation in case preparation and client support.

Outside of work, she enjoys fishing, camping, hiking, and traveling with her husband and two children.

attorneys.name: Daniel P. Beeks
attorneys.firm_name: Bishop, Del Vecchio & Beeks Law Office
attorneys.practice_type: Family Law Lawyers in Phoenix, AZ
attorneys.bio:
Dan Beeks has been an attorney in Arizona for over 20 years. He spent 23 years practicing with prestigious mid-sized and large law firms in Phoenix specializing in commercial litigation. He has extensive experience in nearly all types of complex litigation and appeals, from intellectual property cases to malpractice litigation against brain surgeons, to commercial disputes involving valuation of small and mid-sized businesses. Dan began practicing family law when he and his former partners were frequently retained by other family law attorneys to represent family owned businesses in connection with high net-worth divorces.

Later, because of his extensive experience in handling appeals, he began working with the attorneys at the Bishop, Del Vecchio & Beeks Law Office on appellate matters. He recently joined the Bishop, Del Vecchio & Beeks Law Office where he is primarily practicing family law. Although he works on many complex and high-dollar cases, he frequently enjoys helping people in smaller cases, especially if their former spouses are trying to bully or take advantage of his clients. He still practices other areas of civil litigation as well.

Although Dan typically encourages people to be reasonable, and try to resolve family law disputes in a manner that inflicts as little additional damage on the parties’ family relationships as possible, he also knows that sometimes his opponents and their attorneys are not reasonable. In those situations, there is often no choice but to litigate, and litigate hard. When that happens, Dan works tirelessly, and his years of complex litigation experience become a great advantage to his clients.

Dan has been active in the Arizona legal community for many years. For seven years, he served on the Arizona Supreme Court’s committee in charge of the bar examination, including one year as president. He also served as a hearing officer for the Arizona Supreme Court in attorney discipline cases for approximately ten years. He was also selected by the State Bar of Arizona’s Board of Legal Specialization to serve on the committee in charge of certifying attorneys as specialists in personal injury and wrongful death. He has also been recognized by the Volunteer Lawyers Program as one of the top pro bono attorneys in Maricopa County, for his volunteer legal work with poor clients who could not otherwise afford to pay attorneys.

In his free time, Dan loves to train for and compete in endurance sports. He has run several marathons and half-marathons, and is still dreaming of someday qualifying for the Boston Marathon. This year, he is also training for his first Ironman triathlon. He is the president of the cross country boosters group at his children’s high school, and is a volunteer assistant coach in the summertime with the girls’ distance program.

Awards and Honors

Honors

One of the Top Pro Bono Attorneys in Maricopa County, Volunteer Lawyers Program

Completed the Ironman Arizona Triathlon, 2014 - Present

attorneys.name: Chris H. Begeman
attorneys.practice_type: Contractors and Businesses in Tort Litigation Lawyers in Phoenix, AZ
attorneys.bio:
Chris Begeman is a partner at Righi Fitch Law Group. Mr. Begeman is admitted to practice in Arizona and New Mexico. He handles a wide variety of civil cases, including transportation, construction defect, personal injury, product liability and insurance bad faith. His current practice focuses on defending trucking companies and their drivers in personal injury and property damage matters, individuals and companies involved in injury accidents and construction companies in construction defect and job site injury matters. Mr. Begeman has successfully defended and tried both personal injury and construction defect cases.

Mr. Begeman recently obtained a favorable verdict in a personal injury matter stemming from an automobile accident. Mr. Begeman' s client was extremely intoxicated at the time of the accident. Although liability was conceded, Mr. Begeman was able to convince the jury to award Plaintiff only a day of medical expenses and a nominal amount for pain and suffering. Despite a criminal conviction for operating while impaired, Mr. Begeman successfully argued that punitive damages were not warranted and the jury agreed.

In a construction defect case, Mr. Begeman utilized fee shifting strategy to recover $1.3 million from the plaintiff in a construction defect case. In the case Chris represented a New Mexico general contractor. He advised the contractor to make a strategic settlement offer of 1.3 million. The plaintiff rejected the offer and trial ensued. After securing a full defense verdict, Chris recovered $1.3 million in defense fees and costs from the plaintiff. Mr. Begeman has also successfully defended national home builders in arbitration. Representing a national home builder in a soil movement matter, Mr. Begeman successfully argued that the home had not experienced post construction movement necessitating repairs. The arbitrator agreed and awarded the Claimant less than 2% of Claimants' experts' cost of repair.

Mr. Begeman currently serves on the Executive Committee of the Arizona Association of Defense Counsel. Mr. Begeman also serves as a Member of the Board of Directors for Phoenix Christian PreK-8th Grade School. He is also an active member at Mt. View Presbyterian Church. In his spare time, Mr. Begeman enjoys spending time with his wife and four children, playing softball and everything sports related.

Awards and Honors

Honors

Rising Star, Southwest Super Lawyers Magazine

attorneys.name: Douglas F. Behm
attorneys.practice_type: Litigation Lawyers in Scottsdale, AZ
attorneys.bio:
Mr. Behm has practiced law for more than 35 years. He has extensive trial and appellate court experience. Based in the Phoenix-Scottsdale metropolitan area, he represents clients in complex civil litigation, white collar criminal defense, and corporate compliance throughout the Southwest.

Mr. Behm began his career as an assistant district attorney in Kings County (Brooklyn), New York. He then served as senior trial attorney with the United States Department of Justice Organized Crime and Racketeering Section in New York City for more than nine years, where he prosecuted high profile cases involving criminal RICO, labor racketeering, tax evasion, narcotics trafficking, securities fraud, and official corruption.

Since leaving the government in 1987, Mr. Behm has been a partner in two national law firms, with a five year period as a sole practitioner in between. In his last firm, he was chairman of the litigation department, which included more than 50 attorneys. During his private practice career he has defended corporations, public officials, corporate officers, and individuals in complicated criminal matters; conducted corporate internal investigations; and defended and prosecuted complex civil litigation, including breach of contract, securities fraud, civil RICO, breach of fiduciary duty, and intellectual property cases.

Mr. Behm decided to resume his solo practice in 2008 because he believes it allows him to provide his clients with more personal, more efficient, and more effective representation than was possible in a large law firm. Furthermore, the unusual breadth of both his civil and criminal law experiences gives him exceptional insight into complex civil litigation, regulatory investigations, and criminal cases.

attorneys.bio:
Doug Belknap is a Tennessee transplant who moved to Arizona in 1989 after receiving his law degree and MBA from the University of Tennessee that same year. Doug began his legal career at Gallagher & Kennedy, the prestigious Arizona firm that recruited him west. Doug left G & K in 1994 to practice in a less formal setting.

Since 1994, Doug's practice generally has focused on insurance clients. He maintains relationships with several carriers who rely on him for coverage and bad-faith defense needs. Doug's primary practice area, however, is insurance subrogation. Subrogation allows Doug to leave his office to slog through the damages resulting from fires, floods, drunk drivers who have knocked down houses, and other disasters both natural and man-made. Doug has recovered well over $15 million for his subrogation clients in the past few years.

Trial Experience Counts. Doug firmly believes that virtually all civil disputes can and should be resolved without the time and expense of a trial, and often without the need for a lawsuit. Even in the face of vigorous disagreements about facts or law, competent attorneys and reasonable clients can evaluate the probabilities associated with the universe of possible outcomes and can resolve disputes based upon those probabilities. Doug has tried many cases to juries, however, and has handled many matters in appellate courts. This experience not only allows Doug to analyze how judges or juries might react, but it also gives his clients the confidence that a case will be ready to take to trial if a trial becomes necessary.

Statewide Practice. Although much of Arizona's population is centered in Maricopa County, Doug's practice truly is statewide. In his 24 years of practice Doug has handled cases in every Arizona county and in most of Arizona's cities and towns. He has represented the State of Arizona, Pima County, and the City of Tucson, as well as Maricopa County and the City of Phoenix.

No Question Too Small. Doug's clients universally enjoy his willingness to take phone calls, answer questions, and discuss matters of any sort, regardless whether the issue will lead to a fee. His clients have constant access via email and cell phone. Doug invites contact whenever a client--or anyone else--has a need. If Doug cannot help directly, he always can provide information about another resource.

Other Practice Areas. Although much of Doug's practice involves subrogation or coverage, Doug also handles a variety of matters outside of the insurance world. Doug has several corporate clients to whom he provides advice and assistance. He successfully has represented individuals and families in personal-injury and wrongful death claims, has handled professional malpractice claims, and has been asked to preside over settlement negotiations. Doug also has served as an expert on several insurance issues and has lectured to insurance, governmental, and professional groups on a range of topics.

Go Big Orange. Doug remains an avid supporter of University of Tennessee sports. His two daughters are fantastic athletes who someday may become Volunteers. Long ago, Doug forgave his lovely wife Dana for attending the wrong UT.

attorneys.practice_type: Municipal Corporations and Special Taxing Districts Lawyers in Tucson, AZ
attorneys.bio:
Thomas A. Benavidez is shareholder and President of Benavidez Law Group, P.C. Thomas graduated cum laude from California Western School of Law in 1996. While in law school, Thomas earned the position of Executive Lead Articles Editor for the California Western International Law Journal, remained perpetually on the Dean's List and clerked for Appellate Defenders, Inc., writing appellate briefs, motions, and memoranda. Before becoming a part of the Hochuli & Benavidez, P.C., team in 1996, Thomas interned for the Honorable Rudi M. Brewster, United States District Court Judge, writing bench memoranda and court orders. When Daniel J. Hochuli retired from private practice in January 2006, the firm’s name changed and Thomas became the sole shareholder. Today, Thomas manages the firm and serves as general counsel for numerous local governmental entities. He also represents the firm’s other clients in employment, contract and general litigation matters. Thomas is a graduate of the Arizona College of Trial Advocacy.

Before starting his career in law, Thomas was a competitive rifle shooter. Due to the demands of his family and law practice, Thomas has retired from competition, but still actively participates in shooting sports, competitive kayak bass fishing and hunting.

attorneys.bio:
Lisa graduated from the James E. Rogers College of Law at the University of Arizona in May, 2001, and she has been practicing in the area of family law since 2002. She is a regular participant in family law clinics through Step Up to Justice and through the Pima County Bar Association. She is appointed as both an arbitrator for civil cases and a judge pro tem for family law settlement conferences at the Pima County Superior Court. She often serves as a mediator in family law matters and is committed to helping people work through difficult life transitions with respect and caring.

Outside of the office, Lisa used to keep busy with her own family, but her three children are now adults and largely independent in their jobs and educational pursuits. These days, the family’s goldendoodle joins her on weekend hikes and trail runs. Lisa also enjoys cooking and she attends weekly Swedish classes to keep in touch with her heritage.

attorneys.name: Erik Bergstrom
attorneys.firm_name: Bishop, Del Vecchio & Beeks Law Office
attorneys.practice_type: Lawyers in Phoenix, AZ
attorneys.bio:
Erik Bergstrom focuses his practice on divorce and family law, with an emphasis on complex cases involving business ownership; residential and commercial real estate holdings; and division of investment accounts, retirement plans and pension benefits. Such matters often involve valuations of business interests in limited liability companies, partnerships and corporations; allocation of trust assets; and determining the community or separate property character of all types of real and personal property.

Erik is a Best Lawyers in America® honoree whose family law clients benefit from his experience and track record of success in divorces involving substantial business, professional practice and real property assets. The following cases illustrate the nature and complexity of matters in which Erik has successfully represented family law clients:

Negotiated many settlements involving multi-million-dollar marital estates involving a family businesses, partnership interests and real property holdings.

Negotiated settlement or tried many cases involving business valuations, including dental practices, medical practices, accounting practices and other professional practices.

Obtained the complete dismissal (and an award of attorney’s fees) against a client’s former spouse who sought retroactive modification of child support against established Arizona law.

Obtained the dismissal of a divorce case in which the spouse resided in a foreign country, successfully arguing the applicability of the forum non conveniens doctrine. That doctrine provides that courts may refuse to take jurisdiction over matters in which there is a more appropriate forum or jurisdiction available to the parties.

Obtained the dismissal of a divorce case in which the spouse resided in a foreign country, successfully arguing the applicability of the forum non conveniens doctrine. That doctrine provides that courts may refuse to take jurisdiction over matters in which there is a more appropriate forum or jurisdiction available to the parties.

Successfully represented many clients in complex jurisdictional disputes involving child custody (the Uniform Child Custody Jurisdiction and Enforcement Act, or UCCJEA) and child support (the Uniform Interstate Family Support Act, or UIFSA).

Erik’s possesses significant knowledge in a variety of important divorce, family law and post-decree issues, including:

Divorce (formally known as “dissolution of marriage”), including legal decision-making (custody), parenting time, child support, spousal maintenance, and division of property and debts.

Post-decree matters, including enforcement and modification of decision-making, parenting time, child support, spousal maintenance and property settlements.

Premarital agreements: drafting and enforcement.

Experienced with all types of family law proceedings, including Emergency Hearings, Temporary Orders Hearings, Trials, Post-Trial Motions and Appeals.

Other family law matters, including grandparent’s visitation and in loco parentis visitation.

Substantial experience in complicated interstate custody and child support matters, jurisdictional disputes and issues arising under the Uniform Child Custody Jurisdiction and Enforcement Act and the Uniform Interstate Family Support Act.

Substantial experience with expert witnesses in family law matters, including parental decision-making (custody) evaluations, business valuations, forensic accountings, division of retirement and pension benefits and other financial experts.

Appeals of all types involving family law matters, including Special Actions, Lower Court Appeals, and Petitions for Review, at all levels including Superior Court, the Arizona Court of Appeals and the Arizona Supreme Court.

Erik’s recent divorce-related appeals have involved abuse of discretion and lack of supporting findings in legal decision-making (child custody) and parenting time disputes; grandparent’s visitation and applicable burdens of proof; characterization of jointly titled bank accounts and commingled funds; effect and enforcement of disclaimer deeds; division of military retirement benefits; and proper jurisdiction under the Uniform Child Custody Jurisdiction and Enforcement Act.

attorneys.name: William D. Bishop
attorneys.firm_name: Bishop, Del Vecchio & Beeks Law Office
attorneys.practice_type: Child Support Lawyers in Phoenix, AZ
attorneys.bio:
The founder of the firm, William D. Bishop, has been practicing law for 20 years. Mr. Bishop grew up in Oregon and obtained his Bachelor of Science degree at Willamette University in Salem, Oregon. Mr. Bishop graduated with honors and obtained double majors in both Political Science and Psychology.

While in college, Mr. Bishop received numerous scholarships and was a member of numerous honor societies including Mortar Board and Omicron Delta Kappa. Mr. Bishop received All-American and Academic All-American Wrestling honors during college. Mr. Bishop brings this same dedication and competitive nature to the courtroom.

Mr. Bishop graduated from Arizona State University College of Law. During law school, Mr. Bishop graduated in the top portion of his class, and was selected as a member of the National Moot Court Team. Mr. Bishop received the honor of the Order Of Barristers for outstanding oral advocacy.

After law school, Mr. Bishop worked for large downtown law firms and practiced in the areas of commercial litigation and family law. Since then, Mr. Bishop has focused primarily in the area of family law and divorce. Mr. Bishop's background and commercial litigation experience has given him an advantage over many other family law attorneys with regard to complex financial and property issues.

Unlike many attorneys, Mr. Bishop does not shy away from contested custody cases. Mr. Bishop's background as a psychology major and his self-fulfillment from assisting people with regard to custody and visitation issues assist him in dealing with custody issues head on. When necessary, Mr. Bishop often involves mental health experts in the custody process, especially when the other parent has certain psychological issues or is attempting to alienate the children against his client.

Mr. Bishop receives numerous referrals from other family law attorneys and attorneys who practice in other areas. Mr. Bishop receives referrals in numerous complex and high conflict cases as a result of his reputation as a professional, very thorough and assertive trial attorney.

Certified Specialist

William D. Bishop is a Certified Family Law Specialist by the State Bar of Arizona Board of Legal Specialization and a preeminent rated lawyer in Martindale-Hubbell listings. Mr. Bishop is a former Judge Pro-Tem, Superior Court of Arizona.

Mr. Bishop is named as one of Arizona's Finest Lawyers (www.azfinestlawyers.org). This selection is a peer-reviewed nomination based upon "a demonstrated record of high achievement, excellent legal skills, and a well-earned reputation for integrity". As of 2010, only 6% of all Arizona's attorneys (including practicing attorneys, retired attorneys, judges and law professors) have been selected for such distinction.

attorneys.firm_name: Law Offices of David A. Black PLLC
attorneys.practice_type: Criminal Law Lawyers in Phoenix, AZ
attorneys.bio:
David Black is a Phoenix criminal lawyer. He has years of experience successfully defending clients charged with a wide array of crimes. As a former prosecutor, he understands how the government puts together a criminal case. With knowledge, intelligence, and an aggressive approach to his cases, he is in a unique position to analyze a criminal case, and provide his clients with an honest, intelligent and accurate strategy for their defense.

Mr. Black is an honors graduate of Arizona State University, and received his law degree in 2007 from the UCLA School of Law. From there, he worked at the Maricopa County Attorney's Office. Mr. Black opened his own law firm in 2010, and since that time he has been engaged almost exclusively in the practice of criminal law.

attorneys.name: Melissa Kleminski Bower
attorneys.practice_type: Family Law Lawyers in Peoria, AZ
attorneys.bio:
Calling Melissa “Wonder Woman” is not far off the mark. She worked full time while attending nights at University of Denver Law School. Working her way through law school, she held a variety of jobs from hotel front desk clerk, to legal assistant, to university admissions assistant. During this busy time, Melissa also held externships and volunteered in legal programs.

She was no stranger to hard work. She had already received an undergraduate degree from the University of Arizona. It was in South New Jersey as a Judicial Clerk to a family court judge, her desire to practice family law was solidified upon her return to Arizona.

People around the office know Melissa to be funny, compassionate, and fair. She realizes how challenging divorce and child custody matters can be. She knows that her clients are going through one of the most difficult times in their lives and need to trust that she will be honest and forthcoming about what may or may not happen. Melissa believes in complete honesty, so her clients know what to expect and can prepare. She believes communication is essential for the best possible outcome in the case and keeps each of her clients involved every step of the way. With Melissa as your attorney, be assured she will assist you in reaching a resolution outside the courtroom if possible. Every case is important with unique circumstances.

Outside of the office, Melissa and her husband are want-to-be foodies and adventurers, they travel wherever and whenever they can. During law school, Melissa participated in a month-long summer abroad program that took her to Beijing, China, a truly “humbling experience.” She volunteers with the 'Ask a Lawyer' program and for Habitat for Humanity. Among her favorite things are her kids, photography, and following the D-Backs. Big fans, Melissa, her Dad, and her kids try to make it to at least one D-Backs game a month.

An associate attorney with the Arizona Law Group, Melissa Kleminski Bower has her office at the firm’s Peoria location.

attorneys.name: Elliot Briggs
attorneys.practice_type: Criminal Defense Lawyers in Phoenix, AZ
attorneys.bio:
Elliot Briggs brings extensive prosecutorial experience and dedicated criminal defense expertise to his practice at Grand Canyon Law Group. As a former prosecutor with both the Maricopa County Attorney's Office and Wilson District Attorney's Office in North Carolina, he developed comprehensive courtroom skills through numerous trial proceedings. Mr. Briggs now channels this experience into criminal defense, where he has successfully handled thousands of cases ranging from DUI misdemeanors to complex felony matters, including homicide cases.

Mr. Briggs completed his undergraduate studies in political science at Southern Virginia University, where he demonstrated leadership through active participation in the legal forum while also competing on the university's basketball team. He subsequently earned his Juris Doctor cum laude from North Carolina Central University School of Law. His competitive drive and legal passion consistently translate into optimal outcomes for his clients.

In his role at Grand Canyon Law Group, Mr. Briggs provides comprehensive legal representation to Arizona residents, combining strategic expertise with genuine client advocacy. His approach emphasizes personal connection and transparent communication, offering empathetic guidance while maintaining rigorous professional standards. This client-centered focus aligns with the firm's foundational principles of compassion, integrity, and results-driven representation.

Beyond his legal practice, Mr. Briggs maintains an active lifestyle, particularly through basketball, and prioritizes time with his wife and four children. His commitment to both professional excellence and personal integrity makes him an invaluable asset to clients navigating complex legal challenges.

attorneys.name: Stephen Brower
attorneys.practice_type: Business/Corporate Lawyers in Tempe, AZ
attorneys.bio:
Mr. Stephen Brower is the founder and managing partner of Brentwood Law Group, whose main office is located in Tempe, Arizona. Before he founded Brentwood, Mr. Brower practiced as a business lawyer for distinguished national and regional law firms. He represented high profile corporate and individual clients in complex matters including business litigation, real estate transactions, healthcare consultation, securities 10b-5 litigation, creditors’ rights, and bankruptcy litigation. Mr. Brower aggressively applies and expands his refined skill set to provide cutting-edge legal strategies with a unique “high touch, client centric” approach to legal services.

Mr. Brower recognized early in his career that clients want—and deserve—that unique “trial lawyer mentality” applied to all their legal matters, not just litigation. Mr. Brower applies creative and advocacy-oriented solutions to clients in all areas of his practice, including clients who need a unique approach to their negotiations; contract drafting; business transactions; contract litigation; partnership buyouts; purchase/sale agreements; healthcare entities’ operations, creation, and development; creditor rights, including debt collection; and disputes involving bankruptcy.

Mr. Brower believes that effective planning helps his clients avoid litigation and protects his clients if they are forced to litigate. Mr. Brower negotiates and drafts clear business agreements that position his clients to prevail if their contractual rights are violated. Clients who tap Mr. Brower’s trial experience early in their planning process will experience less disruption in their ventures even if someone breaches their business agreements. And his clients report a sense of relief knowing that they have a battle-tested trial attorney representing their interests in court if they need to assert their rights.

Mr. Brower received his Bachelor of Science in Economics from Arizona State University, graduating summa cum laude. He attended the University of California at Los Angeles, School of Law, where he received his Juris Doctor degree. Mr. Brower is admitted to and has practiced before all Arizona state and federal courts.

attorneys.firm_name: Casey On Your Side – Schmitt Schneck Even & Williams
attorneys.practice_type: Real Estate Lawyers in Phoenix, AZ
attorneys.bio:
Robert Erven Brown, joined the firm as a Member in 2011. Bob focuses on real estate and commercial transactions with a strong emphasis on medical real estate and nonprofit entities including churches and Christian schools. Working closely with nonprofits, Bob helps them manage key operational risks related to their assets, real estate, and campuses. He counsels boards and leadership teams on campus development and construction, entity planning services, and real estate.

Campus Preservation Planning© - Through extensive involvement in the nonprofit sector, Bob developed a unique and comprehensive Campus Preservation Planning© program to protect critical assets of faith-based ministries and secular charities against uninsurable, under-insured, and uninsured unjust claims while simultaneously improving overall risk management and stewardship performance. This program has been successfully implemented across the country.

Beginning with a critical Medicare Cost Appeal in the 1970s, Bob was strategically involved in the evolution of legal and real estate support systems of the hospital holding company for some of the premier retirement communities in the southwestern United States. He assisted in designing innovative joint ventures, prepaid ground leases, a for-profit ancillary company, assisted living facilities, and documented the development and supported the on-going operation, of life care projects.

attorneys.name: Thomas Brown
attorneys.practice_type: Business law Lawyers in Mesa, AZ
attorneys.bio:
Meet Thomas Brown, a skilled problem solver and founding partner of Ernst, Brown, & Draper who works tirelessly to provide his clients with the best possible legal advice and representation. Thomas approaches his work with a focus on creative and effective solutions that align with his clients’ unique needs. Drawing from his strong background in business and finance, Thomas brings a unique perspective to legal issues and enjoys working with clients of all sizes, from start-ups to large corporations. He earned his bachelor’s degree and completed his dual JD/MBA, from Arizona State University, graduating cum lade.

With his extensive knowledge and experience in business and employment law, Thomas has demonstrated an impressive ability to help clients navigate a broad spectrum of legal challenges. These include partnership disputes, non-compete and non-solicit agreements, corporate governance matters, contract disputes, employee handbooks, employment agreements, trade secret and proprietary information issues, as well as discrimination claims and wrongful discharge issues. Throughout his career, Thomas has remained dedicated to finding practical solutions that work best for his clients, making him a reliable and trusted legal advisor. When he’s not working, Thomas enjoys spending time with his wife and seven children and staying active in his community and church. He’s an avid Phoenix Suns and ASU football fan, and enjoys playing chess, camping, and making slow-cooked BBQ on Saturdays.

attorneys.name: Kevin L. Burns
attorneys.practice_type: Criminal Defense Lawyers in Phoenix, AZ
attorneys.bio:
Kevin L. Burns attended law school after receiving his B.S. from the University of Arizona and working in the business community. In 1984 Mr. Burns obtained his J.D. degree from the University of Arizona School of Law. Mr. Burns' legal career began at the Maricopa County Public Defender's Office in Phoenix, Arizona. During his time working at that office Mr. Burns learned and developed his trial skills. Since then, Mr. Burns has continued to refine these skills during his tenure working in the legal community with law firms and governmental agencies.

In 1999 Mr. Burns became a founding member of the law firm Burns, Nickerson and Taylor, PLC. Since then Mr. Burns has further developed and expanded his litigation practice.

His present areas of expertise include all forms of criminal defense along with personal injury, civil rights violations and legal and medical malpractice.

Mr. Burns is a present or past member of Arizona Attorneys for Criminal Justice, Arizona Trial Lawyers Association, American Bar Association, and the American Association for Justice. Mr. Burns is licensed to practice in Arizona State and Federal Courts, along with the United States Court of Appeals for the Ninth Circuit. He is familiar with courts from all Arizona jurisdictions including Municipal, Justice and Superior Courts.

Mr. Burns has resided in Arizona since 1978. He is married with two children both of whom attend school in Scottsdale. He is an outdoor enthusiast who enjoys hiking, camping and golf.

SKILLS

Tried in excess of 50 felony jury trials and many more misdemeanor and bench trials.

Lead attorney on capital cases from inception through sentencing phase. Presently death penalty qualified.

Extensive pretrial motion practice including evidentiary hearings and special actions.

Post-conviction practice including motions for new trials and appeals.

Versed in using Experts including DNA Frye hearing, Competency/Sanity issues and Criminalists.

Strong emphasis on case preparation, including witness interviews/depositions and investigative development.

Team leadership position since 1997 over five attorneys to facilitate the operation of a Superior Court Division and several Justice Courts.

Held half a criminal defense contract for the City of Phoenix since 1999.

attorneys.bio:
Ben is a Certified Specialist in Estate & Trust Law by the State Bar of Arizona and a Certified Elder Law Attorney by the National Elder Law Foundation. Ben has been elected as a Fellow in the American College of Trust and Estate Counsel. He joined Bogutz & Gordon, P.C. in 1999, after having practiced with a Tucson estate planning firm since 1994. He serves on and is past Chair of the State Bar of Arizona Probate & Trust Section Executive Council. Ben earned a B.S. in Commerce from the University of Virginia McIntire School of Commerce, a J.D. from the University of Arizona James E. Rogers College of Law and an LL.M. in Taxation from the University of Denver Sturm College of Law.

He is a Member of the National Academy of Elder Law Attorneys and the Pima County Bar Association. He writes and lectures frequently and is active in numerous community organizations, including formerly serving as Chair of the Board of Goodwill Industries of Southern Arizona, Inc. and as a member of the Board of the Southern Arizona Estate Planning Council. Ben and his wife, Dena, a CPA, have traveled extensively to all seven continents, and they now have two children, Josephine and Ethan, who keep them closer to home.

attorneys.practice_type: Employment Law Lawyers in Mesa, AZ
attorneys.bio:
Miguel A. Cardenas graduated from Arizona State University in Tempe, AZ with a major in Philosophy with a concentration in Politics, Morality, and Law. He earned his Juris Doctor at Western Michigan University Law School and earned the Certificate of Merit for his Trial Skills class and earned the Leadership Award voted by his peers. Miguel served as a student attorney for the Washtenaw County Public Defender Clinic. During his time in Law School he was employed by The Michigan State Attorney General's Office Expungement Unit. He was treasurer of the Health Law Society, a Moot Court competitor, and Board Member of the Student Bar Association.

He joined EBD Lawyers in 2024 as an associate attorney and has worked on a variety of matters in employment and commercial litigation. These include partnership disputes, contract disputes, employee handbooks, employment agreements, trade secret and proprietary information issues, as well as discrimination claims and wrongful discharge issues. In addition to his legal talent, Miguel is known for his strong communication skills, ensuring that clients are well-informed and comfortable throughout the legal process. He approaches each case with empathy and determination, understanding the significance of seeking justice for those who have been wronged.

As the son of Mexican immigrants, he is fluent in Spanish. In his free time, Miguel enjoys spending time with his family, friends and golfing.

attorneys.practice_type: Employment Litigation Lawyers in Mesa, AZ
attorneys.bio:
Mirra Carrier works as a Senior Attorney at Ernst, Brown & Draper and focuses her practice primarily on employment and business law. Prior to joining EBD, Mirra gained valuable substantive knowledge and experience working in employment litigation at a highly regarded Phoenix firm. There, she handled a wide range of cases, including Title VII, ADA, FMLA, employment agreement disputes, and wage claims. Before moving to Arizona, Mirra represented survivors of sexual abuse at a nationally renowned litigation firm in Boston, Massachusetts, where she developed a client-centered approach in handling highly sensitive matters. Mirra has experience litigating in both state and federal trial and appellate courts. She is committed to providing excellent representation to her clients through effective communication and creative problem-solving.

A New York native, Mirra received her bachelor’s degree from Hamilton College and her Juris Doctor from Boston University School of Law. She is admitted to practice in both Arizona and Massachusetts state courts, as well as the U.S. District Courts for Arizona and Massachusetts, and the Ninth Circuit Court of Appeals.

When she’s not working, Mirra enjoys spending time with her husband and their daughter, travelling, and reading 19th century literature.

attorneys.name: Ty Catmull
attorneys.practice_type: Personal Injury Lawyers in Phoenix, AZ
attorneys.bio:
Ty Catmull is an injury attorney specializing in pre-litigation and litigation cases in the Phoenix office of Thompson Law. Ty has dedicated his career to advocating for individuals who have suffered severe injuries or wrongful death. With experience representing thousands of clients, he has successfully recovered millions of dollars in settlements across a variety of cases, including motor vehicle accidents, slip-and-fall incidents, dog bites, wrongful death claims, diminished value claims, workers' compensation cases, and premises liability disputes. His extensive legal expertise spans preventive counseling for corporate in-house counsel, complex bankruptcy transactions, government-sector litigation, and representing clients in private civil matters.

A proud fifth-generation Arizonan, Mr. Catmull graduated from Hamilton High School in Chandler and later earned a bachelor’s degree in Journalism and Mass Communication, Cum Laude, from Arizona State University. During his time at ASU, he reported as a sports broadcaster for the university’s news program, Cronkite Newswatch, and contributed to the Sun Devils 101 series on Fox Sports Arizona. He went on to earn his law degree from the University of Arizona’s James E. Rogers College of Law, where he contributed to the Arizona Journal of International and Comparative Law.

Throughout his legal career, Mr. Catmull has secured over $70 million in settlements for his clients. When he’s not working, he treasures time with his family and enthusiastically supports his favorite Arizona teams—the Suns, Cardinals, Diamondbacks, Wildcats, and Sun Devils—while hoping for a long-awaited championship win.

attorneys.name: Dwane Cates
attorneys.practice_type: Criminal Defense Lawyers in Phoenix, AZ
attorneys.bio:
Dwane Cates has been representing clients in Arizona for over 25 years. Mr. Cates attended Arizona State University where he graduated Suma Cum Laude in Communication, with an emphasis in persuasion. He then attended ASU Law School, (Now Sandra Day O'Conner School of Law.) After graduating, he started his own law firm. Fifteen years ago, he began concentrating primarily on Criminal Law, and was eventually designated as a Criminal Law Specialist by the State Bar of Arizona. In 1999, Mr. Cates was awarded the Tom Karas Award by the State Bar for his contributions to Criminal Law is Arizona.

Mr. Cates has a variety of life experience that helps greatly in his current practice. In his younger days, he used to ride bulls and saddle bronc in rodeos. He worked in the oil fields of Wyoming and was a semi truck driver. He sold cars right before he went back to school later in life. Mr. Cates battled addiction when he was younger but is now clean and sober over 30 years. His website states "experience counts". By that he means both legal and life experience. Dwane Cates is very proud to serve all of Arizona as a Criminal Defense Lawver.

Mr. Cates is a trial lawyer. He bus had great success throughout his career. He tried a murder case on Dateline NBC that was eventually dismissed. Mr. Cates got three jury verdicts overturned between verdict and sentencing. He also got the entire United States Attorney's Office for the District of North Dakota thrown off a case. He represented a person charged with first degree murder in a 30 year old cold case and the person received time served (3.75 years).

Mr. Cates's partner, Aaron Reed, is a great trial lawyer in his own right, having won his last two trials. We are ready to fight for your rights in every Court in the Stale of Arizona.

Honors

State Bar of Arizona Tom Karas Award Winner, Lifetime Achievement Award, 2019 - 2020

attorneys.name: Alan L. Cochran
attorneys.practice_type: Divorce Lawyers in Tempe, AZ
attorneys.bio:
As a quasi-native Arizona resident, although born outside of the state, I attended local schools through high school in Arizona, including Meyer Elementary, Curry Middle School, Connolly Junior High school, McClintock high School in Tempe, Arizona, as well as, Brophy College Prepatory High School in Phoenix through 1980. After graduating high school, I moved to the mid-west where I pursued my undergraduate degree in three years, obtaining academic honors all three years including Red and Black Academic Honor Roll Society for outstanding academic honors and Who’s Who Among College and University Students Academic Honors all three years and graduating in the top 10 percent of my class at Northwestern Oklahoma State University. After getting married and moving to Norman, Oklahoma, I clerked for the Oklahoma Supreme Court for almost four years while moving forward to pursue my law degree at the University of Arkansas School of Law in Fayetteville, Arkansas. The Law School is known for its high academic credentials and renowned faculty including Robert A. Leflar, one of the founding members of Conflicts Law and Law School Dean Emeritus, as well as his son, Professor B. Leflar's teaching and research focused on torts, health law, and related fields.

While attending law school I clerked and worked as an associate attorney for a local law firm in the Fayetteville, Arkansas area, with its main partner acting as my mentor, while running a political campaign against the then Governor of Arkansas, William Jefferson Clinton. After graduating from law school in 1990, I moved to Corona Del Mar, California and practiced law as In-House counsel for a privately held corporation in Fullerton, California. I returned to Arizona in 1993 and also passed the Arizona State Bar exam and eventually moved back to Arizona in 1994 to re-enter private practice concentrated in family law and civil litigation. I moved to Boca Raton, Florida in 1999 and, once again re-entered practice as In-House corporate counsel for a privately held corporation located in 45 cities in 23 states. I moved back to Arizona in 2004 to re-enter private practice including family law and civil litigation for the past ten years, to present.

My method of practicing law includes aggressive compassion with empathy and a desire to do what is right and ethical for my client(s) and their families. I take each matter very personal and will turn over every stone, push and grind all limits of the ethical legal practice to reach the best possible result for you and your children and family, or you and your civil litigation disputes. I am experienced in all aspects of dissolution of marriage, legal decision-making (custody), parenting time (visitation), paternity, child support, spousal maintenance, post-decree modifications, juvenile severance matters, and the difficult and hard to negotiate with client and opposing counsel. My civil litigation experience includes contract disputes, real property and land rights disputes, evictions, real property covenants and restrictions, defense of HOA claims, land line and right-away disputes, and defense of tortious interference of contractual rights and bad-faith property insurance defense claims.

I have research, drafting, and oral argument experience in the Arizona Court of Appeals and Arizona Supreme Court, as well as, significant superior court, justice court and small claims court litigation and trial experience.

Alan Cochran is license in Arizona and Arkansas and is known in the Arizona legal family law community as being a passionate and intelligent advocate for his clients, for being fully informed about his client's cases, a reasonable problem solver, and an effective trial attorney. Alan has spent the last 20 years honing his family law skills and is an effective, compassionate and aggressively proficient family lawyer in the areas of dissolution of marriage (divorce), parenting time (visitation), child support, alimony/spousal maintenance, legal separation, division of assets and debts, paternity, orders of protection, child abuse, community property laws, termination of parental rights and step-parent adoption.

Alan has a 3 ½ year old son that is the center of his life and enjoys going to the train parks, fishing, travel and spending as much time as possible with his son.

attorneys.practice_type: Civil Disputes Lawyers in Tempe, AZ
attorneys.bio:
Jesse D. Cook, is a licensed attorney and an active member of the State Bar of Arizona and the State Bar of Montana. Jesse received his B.A. from Arizona State University and J.D. from the University of South Dakota. While in law school, Jesse served as editor-in-chief of the Great Plains Natural Resources Journal, an environmental law review journal. Jesse also studied German and European Union Law at the University of Munich in Munich, Germany.

After completing law school, Jesse practiced law as an insurance defense attorney in Billings, Montana for several years. There he defended numerous businesses, contractors and individuals who were being sued. After moving back home to Arizona, Jesse has represented both Plaintiffs and Defendants in all sorts of civil disputes. Through his experience of being both a defense and plaintiff’s lawyer, Jesse has gained the insight and experience needed to anticipate what the opposition will do and prepare for every scenario in each case.

Since 2002, Jesse has also owned and operated JDC Sports Management, a sports agency which has represented professional football, baseball and basketball players. Jesse is a certified agent by the Major League Baseball Players Association (MLBPA) and currently represents Major League and Minor League Baseball Players. Jesse is also Registered Athlete Agent by the State of Arizona.

attorneys.name: Lacy A. N. Cooper
attorneys.firm_name: Casey On Your Side – Schmitt Schneck Even & Williams
attorneys.practice_type: Civil Litigation Lawyers in Phoenix, AZ
attorneys.bio:
Prior to joining the firm, Lacy served her community for 15 years as both a county and federal prosecutor. She began her career in Payson, Arizona working as a Deputy Gila County Attorney. In that role, Lacy prosecuted drug dealers, white collar criminals, sexual predators, and others. She received specialized training and experience prosecuting crimes against children, and she participated on a Multi-Disciplinary Team designed to coordinate the efforts of the various entities providing care to child victims. She participated in drafting child abuse investigation protocols and trained law enforcement and community partners on their implementation. Lacy brings this experience to bear when advising churches and other non-profit organizations.

After leaving Gila County, Lacy worked for eight years in the United States Attorney’s Office for the District of Arizona as an Assistant United States Attorney prosecuting gangs, cartels and terrorists. Lacy served as the office’s Border Security Section Chief, Government Ethics Officer, and Anti-Gang Coordinator. Lacy has written numerous appeals and argued before the Ninth Circuit Court of Appeals on three occasions.

During her career, Lacy has appeared as counsel in nearly 100 trials and countless other hearings. Lacy’s significant experience as a criminal litigator in both state and federal court informs her civil litigation practice.

attorneys.practice_type: Family Law Lawyers in Phoenix, AZ
attorneys.bio:
Carrie P. Cravatta is an attorney who represents clients in family law matters in Arizona. She is compassionate, caring, honest and respectful family law attorney.

She grew up in a small town in Illinois, but gravitated towards the "big city" after high school for both college and law school. She attended North Central College in Naperville, Illinois and The John Marshall Law School in Chicago, Illinois. Carrie is licensed in both Illinois and Arizona.

Carrie Cravatta has been recognized by peers and was selected to Super Lawyers for 2021 to the present. Prior to that she was recognized as a Rising Star by Super Lawyers (2016 - 2018). This selection is based off of an evaluation of 12 indicators including peer recognition and professional achievement in legal practice. Being selected to Super Lawyers is limited to a small number of attorneys in each state. As one of the few attorneys to garner the distinction of Super Lawyers, Carrie Cravatta has earned the respect of peers as one of the top-rated attorneys in the nation.

She has also been recognized as one of the "10 Best" Attorneys by the American institute of Family Law and National Academy of Family Law Attorneys. She has presented at several seminars on topics such as Advanced Child and Spousal Support Issues and grandparent visitation, as well as volunteered at the Arizona State University Sandra Day O'Connor College of Law Practice Area Career Fair. Carrie also finds time to volunteer at FLAP often and was recognized for her contributions to FLAP and by the State Bar of Arizona in 2015.

Ms. Crossman is a State Bar Board Certified Workers' Compensation Specialist and is past Co-Chair of the State Bar Workers' Compensation Section. She has served as a faculty member at the State Bar Seminar on Professionalism and is a former Judge Pro Tempore in the Arizona County, Justice, and Superior Courts. According to Martindale-Hubbell, this ranking is a "testament to the fact that a lawyer's peers rank him or her at the highest level of professional excellence." An attorney cannot receive this ranking until he or she has been admitted to the bar for 10 years or more.

In addition, Ms. Crossman was selected for membership in "Arizona's Finest Lawyers." This honor, which is peer-nominated, requires that the attorney demonstrate a commitment to advancing the rule of law, a record of high achievement, excellent legal skills, and a reputation for integrity.

attorneys.name: Benjamin H. Cunningham
attorneys.practice_type: Family Law Lawyers in Chandler, AZ
attorneys.bio:
Family law cases are deeply personal, often life-changing, and always emotionally charged. At Donaldson Stewart, PC, we understand that family law is not just about legal outcomes—it’s about securing a future not just to survive, but to thrive. As a second-career attorney with real-life experience, I bring a unique perspective to my practice. I know what’s at stake, and I fight tirelessly to help my clients navigate these challenging times with confidence.

A Career Built on Dedication & Real-Life Experience

My journey to the legal profession was anything but conventional. I worked full-time while attending law school at night, driven by a relentless work ethic and a passion for advocacy. Before transitioning to family law, I served as a prosecutor in the Family Violence Unit of the Maricopa County Attorney’s Office, where I handled domestic violence, homicide, and child abuse cases. That experience reinforced my commitment to protecting survivors and helping families find stability in the aftermath of difficult circumstances.

A Personal Understanding of Family Law

I don’t just practice family law—I’ve lived it. I’ve been through divorce myself, and I understand the challenges and successes of co-parenting with a former spouse firsthand. In addition, my wife and I are raising two children, including one with special needs. These experiences shape the way I approach my work—with empathy, strategic thinking, and a fierce commitment to securing the best possible outcomes for my clients and their children.

Mediate First. Litigate When Necessary.

At Donaldson Stewart, PC, we believe in pursuing non-litigated dispute resolution whenever possible. However, when litigation is unavoidable, I am a formidable advocate. With a deep command of the rules of evidence and procedure, I have a reputation for being one of the hardest-working attorneys in family law. I excel in trial preparation and strategy, ensuring that my clients are always prepared for the next step.

A Team That Cares | Whole Client Representation

At Donaldson Stewart, PC, we provide whole client representation, understanding that legal battles don’t happen in isolation. My colleagues and I offer a balanced approach—resolving cases amicably when possible and litigating effectively when necessary. Behind the scenes, I work with a world-class staff that is detail-oriented, reliable, and committed to providing exceptional service to our clients. We are known as friendly, ethical, and highly effective professionals who put our clients first.

Let’s Protect Your Future

Whether you’re facing a divorce, custody dispute, or the complexities of co-parenting, you deserve an advocate who understands what’s at stake. Let’s create a legal strategy that protects your rights, your children, and your future. Schedule a consultation today to take the first step toward resolution.

Shawn M. Cunningham devotes his practice to representing clients who have been seriously injured through no fault of their own or who have lost loved ones due to the wrongful conduct or negligence of others. Mr. Cunningham is a member of the Multi-Million Dollar Advocates Forum, a professional organization that recognizes the accomplishments of lawyers who have won million dollar and multi-million-dollar verdicts and settlements for their clients. With his decades of experience, Mr. Cunningham enjoys the highest peer review rating of AV from LexisNexis Martindale-Hubbell, and has been consistently recognized as a premier trial lawyer. Mr. Cunningham is a frequent presenter at seminars. He lives in the Phoenix area and is active in several professional and civic organizations. In his free time, he enjoys skiing, hiking and golf.
