attorneys.practice_type: Litigation Lawyers in Glendale, AZ
attorneys.bio:
Nicholas Darus earned his B.S. in Political Science from the University of California, Santa Barbara in 2008, and his Juris Doctor from the Phoenix School of Law. He began his legal career interning at the Glendale Prosecutor’s Office and clerking for Judge Cohen at the Maricopa County Superior Court.

In 2009, Darus co-founded Darus and Donlan, focusing on litigation including complex business disputes, dissolutions, and criminal proceedings. In 2016, he joined Knochel Law Offices, where he led litigation involving contract and tort claims. By 2021, he became a named partner in the firm, forming Knochel, Knochel & Darus. In 2024, Darus joined Accident Justice, where he now concentrates on personal injury litigation.

Known for his sharp issue-spotting and strategic approach, Darus prides himself on delivering efficient service, comprehensive legal analysis, and client-centered advocacy. He has successfully handled multimillion-dollar cases as well as cases for individuals with modest means. For Darus, it’s not about the size of the case, it’s about achieving the best possible outcome for every client.

Justin R. Davis is a well-seasoned attorney with more than twenty years of experience in counseling and guiding clients through their legal issues. He represents buyers, sellers, developers, and investors in a wide variety of complex commercial transactions, including acquisitions, dispositions, development, land use and entitlements, financing and leasing of improved and unimproved real estate properties for a variety of portfolios. attorneys.bio: DENNIS DeCONCINI is a Shareholder and a founding member of the Firm. He served as Pima County Attorney from January 1972 until mid 1976 when he ran for the US Senate. Mr. DeConcini served in the United States Senate for three terms as a Senator from Arizona. During that time, he served on the Appropriations Committee, Select Committee on Intelligence, Judiciary Committee and the Commission on Security and Cooperation in Europe (Helsinki Commission). Mr. DeConcini received his B.A. from the University of Arizona in 1959 and his LLB from the University of Arizona in 1963. Mr. DeConcini is a member of the Arizona Board of Regents, the State Bar of Arizona, Pima County Bar Association, American Bar Association and District of Columbia Bar Association.

attorneys.name: Paul E. Deloughery
attorneys.practice_type: Business Organizations Lawyers in Phoenix, AZ
attorneys.bio:
Paul Deloughery is a lawyer who finds real-world solutions to real-world problems. He stands against pretense, and advocates on behalf of families.

Paul is founder and senior attorney at Deloughery Law, PLC. He was first admitted to practice law in 1998 and since 2001has focused on estate planning and probate issues, with a strong emphasis on blended families. He graduated with honors from the University of Iowa College of Law in 1996, and was a partner in a home-health agency just before beginning law practice.

Paul sees through complex issues and comes up with potent strategies to resolve his clients' problems.

Consider probate. This can create stress following the death of a loved one. If you're in charge of an estate or trust, all eyes are on you, and people look to you for answers during an emotional time. Greed may enter into it, if a financial windfall is involved. In addition, probate codes are not only complex, they don't come with users' manuals. That's why hiring an experienced attorney is essential. You want guidance. You want answers. You want to get through the process quickly and efficiently. You want Paul. He can help.

On the other hand, estate-planning can be a rewarding experience. Paul brings a breadth of life experience to the task. He can help you decide how you manage your legacy and how you'll be remembered. He'll leave nothing for the family to cope with after the fact.

Paul's own experiences have helped him understand those of others. He knows the pain that family disputes and litigation can cause, and wants to ensure that families don't go through similar situations. He knows firsthand the long-term impact of childhood trauma and family chaos. He has dealt with mental illness and suffered verbal, emotional and even physical abuse. His father died when Paul was 16, and his mother barely escaped bankruptcy. In 2003, when Paul was 35 years old, he discovered that his father had actually been his stepfather. Paul finally met his biological father in 2009, six weeks before his death. Paul has worked hard to overcome this anguished personal history, and has come to a deep understanding of human psychology and the conflicting dynamics underlying legal issues.

attorneys.name: Daniel J. DeRienzo
attorneys.firm_name: Law Office of Daniel J. DeRienzo
attorneys.practice_type: Divorce Lawyers in Prescott Valley, AZ
attorneys.bio:
Daniel J. DeRienzo has over 35 years of legal experience and over 25 years of experience managing a law office. He founded and served as the first Chief Public Defender for Yavapai County from 1998 to 2004. He served as the first President of the Arizona Public Defender's Association and is recognized by his peers as a top notch attorney and litigator.

He is a recipient of the Arizona Attorneys for Criminal Justice William Rothstein Award and in June 2005 was presented with the Arizona Public Defender's Association highest honor, the Gideon Award.

Dan has served with the Arizona Association of Drug Court Professionals and is a member of the National Association of Criminal Defense Attorneys.

He received his Law Degree from the University of Arizona in 1985 and began his career prosecuting securities fraud for the Arizona Corporation Commission. He then served as Deputy County Attorney in Pinal County, AZ, prosecuting DUI's, felonies, and homicide cases. His experience working for the state provided him with trial experience, a valuable tool in defending people charged with criminal offenses as well as presenting divorce cases to the Family Court.

In 1991, Mr. DeRienzo was appointed as Chief Public Defender for the Commonwealth of the Northern Mariana Islands. There he worked with attorneys from across the country and helped draft and write the CNMI statutes. In 1998, he established the first Yavapai County Public Defender's Office and served as Chief Public Defender until 2004.

Since 2004, he has been in the private practice of law. After his own divorce in 2006, Mr. DeRienzo decided to share his experience and decided to practice Family Law. As a result of his own personal experience, he is able to help parents develop a parenting plan which best benefits the children. He is able to bring compassion and understanding to the process of a divorce.

Awards and Honors

Honors

Recipient, Arizona Attorneys for Criminal Justice William Rothstein Award

Highest Honor, Arizona Public Defender's Association, Gideon Award

Arizona Public Defender's Association, First President

attorneys.bio:
Since her admission to the Arizona Bar in 1998, Ms. Dieglio has devoted her practice to criminal defense. During her years with the Pima County Public Defender's Office Ms. Dieglio earned a well deserved reputation as a zealous advocate for her clients. Ms. Dieglio is perhaps best none for her aggressive and thorough motion practice for which she has spoken at several attorney seminars in the past year.

Ms. Dieglio has handled thousands of cases from misdemeanors to serious felony offenses. Ms. Dieglio earned undergraduate degrees in Sociology and Philosophy with an emphasis in law and jurisprudence, as, at that time, she already desired to attend law school and practice criminal defense.

While attending law school at Cleveland State University, and while attending the University of Arizona College of Law as a visiting student, Ms. Dieglio worked for, and learned from, a number highly accomplished "capital offense" criminal defense attorneys.

In order to zealously defend her clients and stay on the cutting edge criminal defense practice, Ms. Dieglio, each year, continues to sharpen her skills and expand her knowledge by attending numerous criminal and dui defense seminars. Ms. Dieglio also has been privileged to attend the Western Trial Advocacy Institute at the University of Wyoming College of Law, an in depth trial trial practice school whose faculty include some of the best criminal defense lawyers in the nation.

attorneys.name: Amy E. Dohrendorf
attorneys.practice_type: Divorce Lawyers in Chandler, AZ
attorneys.bio:
Amy Dohrendorf has wanted to be an attorney as long as she can remember. In fact, she drove her parents a bit crazy as she engaged in debates about everything from current events to curfews to why it wasn't fair for them to force her to eat fish. For graduation, her father framed a newspaper clipping for her that read, "It wasn't anything that you did or didn't do as parents. I was born to be a lawyer."

But why family law? Well, Amy's parents divorced, but they did so amicably and civilly. As a result, she and her brother were well-adjusted, and Amy wanted to help her clients achieve the same positive outcomes for their families. She also once worked for a judge who stressed the importance of knowing your cases backwards and forwards because he had seen so many attorneys arrive at court unprepared. Amy took his advice to heart and even over-prepares for all of her cases. This, of course, is good news for her clients.

This also means that Amy admits to being a bit of a workaholic, but she does manage to find time to stay physically active. While in high school, she played four sports - yes, four - all without losing her honor student status. Today, she enjoys snow skiing when she gets the chance and trains with the Boot Camp Babes. She joined them in the Susan G. Komen 3-day walk to raise money for breast cancer research, helping her team collect more than $80,000.

Amy received a Bachelor of Science degree in Communications cum laude from Northern Arizona University and her Juris Doctorate from the University of Denver. She was on the Dean's List and received a Harold C. Lawson Memorial Law Scholarship. Before joining our firm, she served as Deputy Public Defender in the Maricopa County Public Defender's Office for three years and spent two years in private family law practice.

Besides law, Amy admits to just two obsessions - the Phoenix Suns and Starbucks. She can't get enough of her favorite team, and every morning for the last four years, she has ordered a delicious iced venti unsweetened iced coffee. (Now you know her weakness.)

attorneys.name: Monica H. Donaldson Stewart
attorneys.practice_type: Family Law Lawyers in Chandler, AZ
attorneys.bio:
Practical Experience. Strategic Resolution.

Monica Donaldson Stewart is the managing attorney at Donaldson Stewart, P.C., where she focuses exclusively on family law, helping clients navigate prenuptial agreements, divorce, legal separation, parenting time, child support, and other complex transitions with clarity and confidence.

With nearly three decades of experience, Monica brings a calm, strategic approach to each case. Her goal is simple: to help clients resolve their family law matters efficiently and respectfully.

A Focus on Settlement

Monica is a trained mediator and collaborative divorce professional. She has served as a Judge Pro Tem for the Maricopa County Superior Court since 2007, where she has conducted more than 150 settlement conferences in family law matters. This resolution-focused perspective allows her to see cases from all sides—and helps her clients reach practical, long-lasting agreements without unnecessary conflict. Monica believes litigation should be a last resort, not a default strategy.

Education and Credentials

- Arizona State University, B.S., Political Science, summa cum laude (1993)

- Arizona State University, J.D. (1997)

- Bar Admissions: Arizona State Courts and U.S. District Court, District of Arizona (1997)

Monica began her legal career with a strong foundation in mediation, completing a semester-long clinic during law school. She completed her first collaborative divorce training in 2009 with the Collaborative Divorce Institute and has continued advanced training in the years since.

Leadership and Recognition

Monica is a respected leader in the legal community. She is a member of the Collaborative Professionals of Phoenix and her past service includes:

- President, East Valley Bar Association (2008–09)

- Treasurer, East Valley Bar Association (2010–19)

- Secretary, East Valley Bar Association (2020–21)

- Secretary, Maricopa County Association of Family Mediators (2018–20)

- Board of Legal Specialization, State Bar of Arizona (2009–2020)

She has been recognized by Super Lawyers as a Southwest Rising Star (2012–2013) and has been named a Southwest Super Lawyer every year since 2019.

Beyond the Office

Monica’s blended family includes her husband, six adult children and several four-legged family members. She enjoys nature photography, is an avid reader and is a published author of several novels. Monica understands that life is complex, and she believes that the legal process shouldn’t make it harder.

sections.title: Overview
sections.content:
Practical Experience. Strategic Resolution.

Monica Donaldson Stewart is the managing attorney at Donaldson Stewart, P.C., where she focuses exclusively on family law, helping clients navigate prenuptial agreements, divorce, legal separation, parenting time, child support, and other complex transitions with clarity and confidence.

With nearly three decades of experience, Monica brings a calm, strategic approach to each case. Her goal is simple: to help clients resolve their family law matters efficiently and respectfully.

A Focus on Settlement

Monica is a trained mediator and collaborative divorce professional. She has served as a Judge Pro Tem for the Maricopa County Superior Court since 2007, where she has conducted more than 150 settlement conferences in family law matters. This resolution-focused perspective allows her to see cases from all sides—and helps her clients reach practical, long-lasting agreements without unnecessary conflict. Monica believes litigation should be a last resort, not a default strategy.

Education and Credentials

- Arizona State University, B.S., Political Science, summa cum laude (1993)

- Arizona State University, J.D. (1997)

- Bar Admissions: Arizona State Courts and U.S. District Court, District of Arizona (1997)

Monica began her legal career with a strong foundation in mediation, completing a semester-long clinic during law school. She completed her first collaborative divorce training in 2009 with the Collaborative Divorce Institute and has continued advanced training in the years since.

Leadership and Recognition

Monica is a respected leader in the legal community. She is a member of the Collaborative Professionals of Phoenix and her past service includes:

- President, East Valley Bar Association (2008–09)

- Treasurer, East Valley Bar Association (2010–19)

- Secretary, East Valley Bar Association (2020–21)

- Secretary, Maricopa County Association of Family Mediators (2018–20)

- Board of Legal Specialization, State Bar of Arizona (2009–2020)

She has been recognized by Super Lawyers as a Southwest Rising Star (2012–2013) and has been named a Southwest Super Lawyer every year since 2019.

Beyond the Office

Monica’s blended family includes her husband, six adult children and several four-legged family members. She enjoys nature photography, is an avid reader and is a published author of several novels. Monica understands that life is complex, and she believes that the legal process shouldn’t make it harder.

attorneys.name: Ashley Donovan
attorneys.practice_type: Family Law Lawyers in Tempe, AZ
attorneys.bio:
Ashley Donovan received a B.A. degree in International Affairs from George Washington University in 2004. In 2007, she graduated cum laude from the New England School of Law. While at the New England School of Law she was an Executive Articles Editor of the New England Law Review, and served as a judicial intern for the Honorable Spencer Kagan of the Middlesex Family and Probate Court in Cambridge, Massachusetts.

Prior to forming Ashley Donovan Law, PLLC in 2013, Ms. Donovan worked for a local firm, where she handled complex divorce, custody, support, and juvenile matters. Ms. Donovan was also a Staff Attorney in the Family Law Unit of Community Legal Services, in downtown Phoenix. While there, she represented indigent clients and victims of domestic violence with problems involving divorce, child custody, pre and post decree modifications, relocation, and child support. In addition to litigation, Ms. Donovan served as an advocate for indigent clients and victims of domestic violence.

Ashley was featured in the September 2008 issue of Arizona Attorney magazine. Ashley serves as a judge pro tempore and regularly mediates family court cases. She performs volunteer work through the Family Law Assistance Program and teaches family law related classes at Fresh Start Women's Foundation. Ashley is the past Chair of the Family Law Rules and Procedures Committee through the State Bar of Arizona. She also previously served on the Board of Directors for Free Arts of Arizona.

attorneys.practice_type: Commercial and Civil Litigation Lawyers in Mesa, AZ
attorneys.bio:
Allan Draper is a founding partner of Ernst, Brown & Draper, PLLC. Allan has diverse commercial and civil litigation experience. Allan worked in the commercial litigation department of Greenberg Traurig shortly after graduating from the Sandra Day O’Connor College of Law at Arizona State University. For the past seven years, Allan has been involved in starting multiple successful companies.

During this time, Allan has refined his business expertise and acumen, and has founded several multimillion dollar businesses. Allan owns businesses in the following sectors: home services, product development, real estate, software, digital marketing, lending, investing, and media.

In addition to his successful entrepreneurial endeavors, Allan advises startups, owns a consulting business, and has two business-related podcasts that each release weekly episodes.

Allan’s unique blend of litigation and entrepreneurial experience makes him an asset to every business that retains the firm. Allan’s perspective allows him to advise business clients regarding both legal and business issues while taking into account the client’s long-term goals.

Allan enjoys spending time with his wife and three children. Allan is also active in his church and enjoys going to the gym, golfing, playing basketball, snow skiing, traveling and the occasional game of chess.

attorneys.name: Virginia K. Draus
attorneys.practice_type: Birth Injuries Lawyers in Phoenix, AZ
attorneys.bio:
Virginia K. Draus joined Harris, Powers & Cunningham as an Associate Attorney in the fall of 2025, bringing a diverse professional background and strong commitment to advocacy.

Virginia earned her Bachelor of Science in Psychology from Georgia College & State University, where she also trained as a classical vocalist. She went on to earn her Juris Doctor, graduating cum laude, from the Sandra Day O’Connor College of Law at Arizona State University in 2021. During law school, she received a Certificate in Trial Advocacy and was awarded the Highest Pro Bono Distinction for her dedication to public service. Virginia also distinguished herself through her academic achievements, earning CALI Excellence for the Future Awards in Professional Responsibility and White Collar Crime, and was selected to serve as a Teaching Assistant for Securities Regulation. Virginia was an active member of her law school community, competing in the Kaufman Memorial Securities Law Moot Court Competition and the Health Law Regulatory & Compliance Competition. She participated in the Women’s Law Student Association, sang with Law Cappella, volunteered as an instructor for CourtWorks, and was elected as a representative to the Student Bar Association.

After graduation, Virginia gained extensive courtroom experience as a Deputy County Attorney with the Maricopa County Attorney’s Office and later as an Assistant City Prosecutor for the City of Mesa. Her caseload was predominantly composed of vehicular crimes and crimes of domestic violence. Most recently, she worked for a local defense firm, representing licensed healthcare providers and institutions in medical negligence and wrongful death matters.

Virginia lives in the Phoenix metropolitan area with her husband and their two sons. Outside of work, she enjoys reading, live music, and camping and off-roading adventures with her family.

attorneys.firm_name: Law Office of Chris Dutkiewicz, P.C.
attorneys.practice_type: Bankruptcy Lawyers in Gilbert, AZ
attorneys.bio:
In 2001, I graduated from Brigham Young University with a degree in English. After spending time teaching elementary education in southern California, I entered law school and graduated from Western State University, College of Law in 2006.

While attending law school, I worked full-time at a mid-sized insurance defense firm in Orange County California. This experience allowed me to have hands-on training in multiple aspects of civil litigation, from writing and responding to various motions, to being responsible for large discovery projects on multi-million dollar litigation projects, including one of the firm's most ambitious projects, the defense of a high profile client that resulted in a $110 million dollar settlement.

Upon arriving in the great state of Arizona with my wife, I found employment at a local firm in Gilbert and focused on bankruptcy and estate planning. The firm was bustling with business and offered me daily opportunities to learn new concepts and refine my skills. When the time was appropriate, I began my own practice with the intent of providing help and assistance with bankruptcy, foreclosure, and estate planning issues to residents of the East Valley, including Gilbert, Mesa, Chandler, Queen Creek, and Tempe, as well as Phoenix.

When I'm not helping people achieve debt relief or plan for their children's future, I enjoy spending time with my family, playing basketball, and reading.

attorneys.name: Dorian Eden
attorneys.practice_type: Family Law Lawyers in Phoenix, AZ
attorneys.bio:
My family law practice includes all aspects of dissolution of marriage or divorce cases, such as child custody and support matters, spousal maintenance or alimony, division of assets and debts. In addition, I handle issues that parties need to resolve after their divorce, known as post-decree matters. Before people get married, I will help them with prenuptial or premarital agreements. I firmly believe that the vast majority of cases should end with a negotiated settlement, but I also regularly appear in court for hearings and trials when issues cannot be resolved by mutual agreement of the parties. I handle cases from the very beginning through the trial. In addition, I draft appellate briefs and argue cases before the Arizona Court of Appeals.

In representing clients, lawyers must learn more about them than just about anyone else the clients deal with. This is particularly true in family law cases. It is important that clients feel comfortable with their attorney. So, a little about me: originally from the Chicago area, I graduated from the University of Illinois at Urbana-Champaign. During college, I decided to explore and expand beyond my Midwestern roots, spending summers working as an intern in Washington, D.C. and clerking for judges in Phoenix and Sacramento. I returned to the Midwest for law school, attending Case Western Reserve University School of Law where I graduated cum laude. I am AV Rated by Martindale-Hubbell.

After shoveling one too many driveways in the Midwest, I packed up the day after graduation from law school and drove to Phoenix, where I have lived ever since. I began my legal career at Tiffany & Bosco, P.A., first as an associate and then as a partner. I then moved to The Law Offices of Scott David Stewart, PLLC. In 2012, I decided my clients would be better served if I opened my own firm. Partnering first with Amy and later Carrie were obvious choices to grow the firm. I love Phoenix, the desert and all the great outdoor activities Arizona has to offer. I am very active in the community and served on the Ahwatukee YMCA Board of Managers from 2013-2023 and National Charity League Ahwatukee Chapter Board from 2021-2023. I remain active in National Charity League and very much enjoy being able to give back through volunteer work.

attorneys.name: Brian L. Ellexson
attorneys.practice_type: Social Security- Disability Lawyers in Phoenix, AZ
attorneys.bio:
Brian L. Ellexson is a Phoenix native. He graduated magna cum laude from The University of Arizona in 2003, where he received degrees in Family Studies/Human Development and Spanish, and graduated cum laude from Brooklyn Law School in 2008. In New York City, Brian practiced at a boutique law firm in the areas of trusts and estates; commercial and residential real estate; and complex civil litigation. Upon returning to Arizona in 2010, Brian worked as a solo practitioner counseling individuals and families on estate plans, probate and trust disputes, and general litigation. He joined the Slepian Law Office in 2011.

Brian has studied Social Security Disability Law and has represented claimants at the Office of Disability Adjudication & Review. He has successfully handled Social Security Disability claims and is dedicated to assisting individuals who cannot work. Brian remains involved with The University of Arizona and is involved with The Association for Frontotemporal Degeneration, an organization dedicated to promoting and funding research, increasing awareness, and supporting individuals and families facing frontotemporal degeneration. He volunteers his time with Wills for Heroes, an organization that provides essential legal documents to first responders throughout the Valley.

Brian is admitted to practice law in the states of Arizona and New York. He practices exclusively Social Security Disability Law.

attorneys.name: Benjamin K. Erlick
attorneys.practice_type: Intellectual Property Law Lawyers in Phoenix, AZ
attorneys.bio:
Benjamin Erlick is a patent attorney "of counsel" to Sanders & Parks. He is also Chief Operating Officer of BCMT Enterprises LLC, an advertising company that focuses on Search Engine Marketing (SEM).

He has received Martindale-Hubbell's highest AV Preeminent rating (5.0/5.0), has been recognized by Southwest SuperLawyers as an Arizona Rising Star each year for the last four years (2014-2017), and has an AVVO attorney rating of "Superb" (10.0/10.0).

His law practice is primarily focused in the areas of intellectual property law and civil litigation, including trademark law, trade secrets, patent litigation, and construction defect litigation.

Trademarks

Mr. Erlick's trademark practice includes:

Trademark infringement litigation

Counseling clients on legal issues to consider when creating and selecting trademarks,

Trademark searching to identify potential issues,

Registration of trademarks, and

Renewal of trademarks (including filing section 8 declarations of continued use, section 9 applications for renewal, and section 15 declarations of incontestability).

Patents

Mr. Erlick has been licensed to practice before the United States Patent and Trademark Office (USPTO) since 2002, initially as a Patent Agent and currently as a Patent Attorney. He has experience in both of the two major areas of patent practice:

Patent prosecution (including determining whether innovations and technologies may be patentable, drafting and filing applications to obtain patents in the United States and in other countries throughout the world, and responding to office actions to overcome patent examiners' objections and rejections), and

Patent litigation (including filing or defending lawsuits involving alleged patent infringement, or resolving potential patent related conflicts and issues through licensing or alternative methods of dispute resolution).

Mr. Erlick's intellectual property experience covers a wide variety of technical fields, including: mechanical, electromechanical, computer software, semi-conductor hardware, alternative energy, communications, medical devices, and business methods. He is a registered Professional Engineer (P.E.) in Arizona, with proficiency in civil engineering. He also has a Masters degree in business administration.

Mr. Erlick's patent litigation practice includes:

Infringement analysis (evaluating whether a particular patent may be infringed by a particular product, apparatus, method, or process, etc.). This involves analyzing the scope of patent claims defined by the claim elements in conjunction with the teachings of the specification, and determining whether the alleged infringing product embodies/practices all the claimed elements of the patent.

Invalidity analysis (evaluating whether a facially valid and issued patent may ultimately be held invalid and unenforceable as a result of defects in the patent, such as inventorship issues, indefiniteness, anticipation or obviousness due to prior art, insufficient enablement, or other issues).

Mr. Erlick is also available to counsel clients on whether there may be legal and effective ways to work around or design around particular patents to avoid infringement, or whether a patent has broad enough claims to encompass, and therefore prevent, a particular workaround.

Additional Background

In law school, Mr. Erlick was elected President of the Student Bar Association, and was appointed Chief Justice of the Honor Court, Managing Editor of the Phoenix Law Review, and Chair of the Moot Court Honor Board. He was also a member of the intellectual property law society.

attorneys.name: Joshua Ernst
attorneys.practice_type: Business Contracts And Disputes Lawyers in Mesa, AZ
attorneys.bio:
Joshua Ernst is a named partner of Ernst, Brown & Draper, PLLC. In private practice at a large Phoenix firm, Joshua represented clients in complex commercial litigation cases, including breach of contract, fraud, misappropriation of trade secrets, and insurance subrogation claims. In addition, Joshua has also represented parties in wrongful termination, wage and hour disputes, and defensed employers against EEOC charging letters. Joshua has practiced in Maricopa County Superior Court, Arizona District Court, the Arizona Court of Appeals and the Arizona Supreme Court, including drafting a successful Petition for Review to the Arizona Supreme Court, ultimately leading to a successful decision in his client’s favor. For the past five years, Joshua has served as in-house litigation counsel for Salt River Project Agricultural Improvement and Power District. While there, Joshua defended multiple personal injury, property damage, and wrongful death claims, as well as unique antitrust and other statutory issues. Joshua’s time in-house deepened his appreciation and ability to get to a workable solution that takes into account the relevant risks, benefits, and importantly, costs to achieve his client’s desired results. While at SRP, Joshua regularly met with executive-level management to provide practical legal advice and provide recommendations on how various business groups might accomplish their goals. Joshua understands that running a business requires a certain level of risk, and he takes pride in partnering with business owners to minimize those risks where possible and defending his clients’ interests when necessary.

Joshua is heavily involved with his family and church, and enjoys spending time with his wife and five children.

attorneys.name: Giancarlo G. Estrada
attorneys.practice_type: Estate Planning Lawyers in Phoenix, AZ
attorneys.bio:
Mr. Estrada focuses on estate planning, elder law, and closely related practice areas. His approach to the practice of law begins with the very basic idea that family is your most important asset. The reason why most people consider any type of planning is because they have a desire to make things easier, whether emotionally or financially, for their family members.

Mr. Estrada enjoys estate planning because unlike other areas of the law, it represents a pro-active positive step in caring for loved ones. He derives a great deal of personal and professional satisfaction from serving as a trusted advisor to his clients. He takes the time to get to know his clients personally, explain all their planning options, and make sure that they understand the plan he creates for them.

The Importance Of Family

Mr. Estrada was fortunate to grow up in an extended family, one that included four living generations and varied cultures. This allowed him to see the many challenges inherent in issues like aging or divorce. When his great-grandmother began experiencing early signs of Alzheimer's, his family struggled with striking a balance between preserving her independence, protecting her physical well-being, and finding the care she needed. In short, Mr. Estrada knows first hand the importance of long-term care planning and estate planning, as well as the emotions families face when trying to make difficult decisions.

attorneys.bio:
Dennis Evans is a Social Security Disability lawyer at the law offices of Dayes Law Firm PC, on counsel for Phillips Law Group. Mr. Evans joined Dayes Law Firm after having served in one of the largest disability law firms in the United States.

With members of his own family being disabled and at one point, being unable to obtain the help they needed to secure benefits, Mr. Evans brings a unique perspective to our law firm and provides compassionate and comprehensive legal services to his clients. Mr. Evans studied Business Administration and Human Resource Management at California State University in Sacramento. Mr. Evans studied law at The University of San Diego, where he received his Juris Doctorate and LL.M in Taxation. Mr. Evans has successfully represented thousands of clients in front of the Social Security Administration.

These unique insights help Dennis to understand the needs of each claim and to determine the level of support that each client needs. Dennis is admitted to practice in California, outside of California, limited to Social Security Disability practice and Federal Administrative law.

When he’s not helping others, Mr. Evans is a dedicated family man that enjoys spending time with his wife and four sons.

Ms. Fenlon earned her B.S. in Foreign Service from the Georgetown University School of Foreign Service in 1981. She then graduated from the Thunderbird School of Global Management, Garvin Center, with a Master's Degree in International Management in 1983. Her studies at Thunderbird focused on international finance.

She graduated from the Sandra Day O'Connor College of Law at Arizona State University in 1990. While in law school, Ms. Fenlon taught as a writing instructor and was a property tutorial instructor. She is licensed to practice law in the state and federal courts of Arizona, and the Ninth Circuit Court of Appeals.

During the last several years, Ms. Fenlon has been a member of the State Bar of Arizona, the Maricopa County Bar Association, the Scottsdale Bar Association, and the Arizona Women Lawyers Association. attorneys.name: Rachelle S. Ferraro
attorneys.firm_name: Law Office of Rachelle S. Ferraro
attorneys.practice_type: Criminal Traffic Violations Lawyers in Phoenix, AZ
attorneys.bio:
Rachelle S. Ferraro is a Wellesley College graduate originally from New Jersey who has settled down in Phoenix, Arizona after having obtained her Juris Doctor Degree at the University of Arizona in 1998. Certified as a Criminal Law Specialist by the Arizona State Bar Board of Specialization, she stands out at the top of her field of practice. Ms. Ferraro has tried in excess of seventy (70) jury trials in local, state and federal court and has obtained Not Guilty verdicts and dismissals in rape, kidnapping, drug sales, aggravated assaults, DUIs and many other areas. Because she also gets involved before charges are filed whenever possible, she has been able to prevent charges from being filed in aggravated assault, money laundering, sexual assault, and many other situations.

Advocate for the Wrongly Accused and for those who Deserve a Second Chance.

Ms. Ferraro has practiced criminal defense since her admission to the Arizona State Bar and the Arizona District Court in 1998. She has never prosecuted for any agency but has always defended and truly believed in protecting the rights of those accused and persecuted by the State and the Government. Her clients include those innocent individuals who have been wrongly accused and those who, due to circumstances beyond their control or poor decisions, deserve a second chance. Ms. Ferraro believes it is her duty to hold the State, the Police, the Prosecution and the Courts to the constraints of the Constitution and to present a different version or perspective than has been considered by the Prosecution and the Courts.

Misdemeanor and Felony Criminal Defense Practice.

Ms. Ferraro's practice includes the defense of criminal traffic violations, DUIs, domestic violence offenses, all misdemeanor offenses including thefts, assaults, disorderly conduct, criminal damage, contempt, violations of orders of protection, graffiti and all felony offenses, including computer crimes, crimes of violence, identity theft crimes, sexual offenses, aggravated assaults, thefts, weapons charges, drug offenses, and homicides. Ms. Ferraro accepts representation of individuals before they are charged, while their cases are pending and after conviction for sentencing, appellate or post-conviction relief, probation violations/modifications/early terminations, restoration of civil rights and the setting aside of convictions.

Certified Criminal Law Specialist

Ms. Ferraro has been certified as a Criminal Law Specialist by the Arizona Board of Legal Specialization in 2006 and maintains that certification. She practices in all cities and jurisdictions in Maricopa County including but not limited to Phoenix, Scottsdale, Paradise Valley, Tempe, Mesa, Chandler, Gilbert, Cave Creek, Carefree, Fountain Hills, Peoria, Glendale, Surprise, Avondale, Goodyear; and in outlying counties including Pinal and Yavapai Counties and surrounding areas.

attorneys.name: Lowell W. Finson
attorneys.practice_type: Personal Injury Lawyers in Phoenix, AZ
attorneys.bio:
Mr. Finson is an attorney licensed to practice in California, Arizona and Ohio. He has over 40 years of trial and appellate experience representing consumers on all types of serious personal injury matters including auto, truck, motorcycle and work injuries.

Mr. Finson received his BSBA with honors and distinction from Miami University in 1971 and he is also a 1974 Cum Laude graduate of Marshall School of Law at Cleveland State.

Mr. Finson began practicing law in 1974, focusing on personal injury, medical malpractice, product liability, employment law and workers’ compensation.

In 2004, he was asked to form a mass tort drug and device litigation department with Phillips Law Group in Phoenix. Along with his wife Karen Finson, a doctor of pharmacology, he created a department, managing 14 employees, 4 attorneys, and grew the department to 15,000 cases. In 2011, Mr. Finson took the California Bar, and the department was moved to Los Angeles. Mr. Finson is still based in the Los Angeles office today and is “Of Counsel” to Phillips Law Group.

Mr. Finson has been litigation counsel in many California Federal and state drug and device mass tort cases, including Crestor, Avandia, Vioxx, Bextra, Celebrex, TVM, Infuse Bone Graft, Shoulder Pain Pump, Yasmin, Ortho-Evra Patch, Gadolinium, Zyprexa, Nuvaring, Pseudo Tumor Cerebri, Actos, Accutane, Hernia Mesh, Mirena, Sitagliptin, Januvia, Fosamax, Risperdal, Inovkana, Taxotere, Pinnacle and Depuy Hip litigations.

Mr. Finson is admitted to all Federal and State courts in California, Arizona and Ohio. He was also specially admitted in United States District Courts in Texas, New York, Louisiana, Kansas, Missouri, Florida, Pennsylvania, New Jersey, Ohio, South Carolina, Massachusetts and West Virginia, as well as in the United States Courts of Appeals in the Second, Fifth, Sixth and Ninth Circuits. He has tried over 200 jury trials to conclusion in Ohio, Arizona and California, and has handled over 3000 arbitrations and other administrative hearings.

Mr. Finson is now actively involved in hundreds of individual opioid cases and has been active in consulting with firms across the country to file individual Opioid cases to assist those whose lives have been ruined by these dangerous drugs.

Lowell’s “Why”

When I was in high school, doing debate and speech, it was clear to me I wanted to be a lawyer. From that day, I never waivered from my goal, finishing undergraduate and law school without taking time off to go in any other direction. Medical injuries can be life altering, and those who suffer must have a voice. I am honored to be that voice.

attorneys.name: Elizabeth S. Fitch
attorneys.practice_type: Insurance Defense and Bad Faith Litigation Lawyers in Phoenix, AZ
attorneys.bio:
Elizabeth S. Fitch is a founding member of Righi Fitch Law Group. She is a trial attorney with over 28 years of civil defense experience and has the AV Preeminent Rating. Beth has defended numerous multi-million dollar cases ranging from catastrophic injuries to construction defect cases. She has represented all types of professionals from lawyers to architects. Because of her defense of insureds under general liability insurance policies, Beth has successfully handled the entire gamut of complex tort cases ranging from construction mishaps to wrongful death to sexual harassment. She has been featured twice in Attorney At Law and co-authored the Construction Defect chapter of the Arizona State Tort Law Handbook. In 2014 she was again recognized as a Super Lawyer and inducted into Arizona's Finest Lawyers.

Her practice has concentrated on representing businesses and individuals in complex civil litigation matters. The nature of complex litigation not only requires experience and knowledge about the substantive law but also requires sophistication in addressing the interrelated contractual and complex insurance issues. She has developed expertise in risk management and assists clients with risk transfer strategies such as pursuing indemnity and primary, excess, and additional insurance coverage for clients.

Beth focuses her time working with clients on strategic planning for the complex cases. Recognizing that clients are best served by quick resolution of cases, at the outset of every case she looks for innovative solutions that bring about the client's desired result in an economical and expedient manner.

Beth is certified by the International Association of Privacy Professionals. The CIPP/US certification is the preeminent privacy credential in the US private sector. Beth serves as the Chief Information Security Officer for her law firm. Beth counsels companies and insureds on cyber liability and responding to data breaches. Beth coordinates the Cyber Early Response Team for Themis Advocates Group and is published on Cyber liability risks.

Beth is a third generation Arizonan and comes from a long line of entrepreneurs. Her great grandmother founded successful wholesale and retail businesses. Her dad followed in this tradition and started a successful retail business and cattle ranch. As a result she understands the business needs of clients and applies entrepreneurial principles to her practice.

attorneys.bio:
Steve Ford's practice focuses on successfully addressing the litigation and strategic needs of businesses and the individuals who own, operate, and work with such entities. The majority of Mr. Ford's practice is devoted to representing both plaintiffs and defendants in civil and commercial litigation matters in state and federal courts, as well as in arbitration and other dispute resolution settings. Steve handles all phases of litigation, including identifying and developing claims and defenses, preparing necessary and appropriate filings, conducting effective discovery, motion practice, and other pre-trial tasks, and presenting cases to judges, arbitrators, and juries.

As part of his practice, Mr. Ford advises individuals and businesses in contract and entity formation, preservation and prosecution of their business interests, and litigation avoidance and strategy. Mr. Ford is able to draw on his diverse experience representing clients with unique legal needs in a wide variety of settings. This experience, including his years with a large national law firm, allows Steve to provide top-tier legal advice with the added benefits of highly personalized attention and one-on-one service.

Steve has called the Valley home for over 40 years and attended elementary school, junior high, and high school in Tempe. In 1995, he graduated cum laude from the Arizona State University College of Law (now known as the Sandra Day O'Connor College of Law), and before entering private practice, served as a law clerk to the Honorable Thomas C. Kleinschmidt and the Honorable Michael D. Ryan during their respective tenures on the Arizona Court of Appeals. Steve is licensed in Arizona state and federal courts and in the Ninth Circuit Court of Appeals, and is a member of the Arizona State Bar, the Maricopa County Bar Association, and the Scottsdale Bar Association.

attorneys.name: Lucas Frei
attorneys.practice_type: Vehicle Accidents Lawyers in Phoenix, AZ
attorneys.bio:
Lucas Frei is an attorney with Phillips Law Group with experience in many areas of law, including tax controversy and litigation, tax planning, estate planning, probate, immigration, business law, and personal injury.

Lucas was born and raised in Gilbert, Arizona, and earned his Bachelor of Science from Northern Arizona University. He went on to earn his Juris Doctorate degree from the Sandra Day O’Connor College of Law at Arizona State University before pursuing his LL.M. – Master of Laws Degree (Taxation) from the University of Denver.

Licensed in both Arizona and Colorado, Lucas prides himself on client service and on being available to his clients and getting them the results they deserve.

Lucas is married to his wife, Michelle, who is also an Arizona native, and they share two spoiled black labs that are both rescues. He is a big fan of all things Arizona sports, and cheers for the Cardinals, Suns, Diamondbacks, Coyotes, Phoenix Rising, and more.

In his free time, Lucas enjoys traveling – particularly in his home state and in the southwest as a whole – and takes frequent day trips with his wife. He also loves to cook.

Lucas’ “Why”

There are unfortunately a lot of unsavory businesses and individuals out there that will take advantage of people when they are at their most vulnerable. Personally, I was the passenger in a car accident when I was younger, and dealing with the insurance company was a nightmare. I didn’t use an attorney, and I settled with them, but found out later that the insurance company should have paid me substantially more than they did.

I became an attorney to protect myself, my family, and my clients because they could end up in similar positions where the government, big businesses, or other individuals with bad motives may try to take advantage of them.

Further, I recognize that people often make mistakes, and sometimes they just need a bit of help to get back on their feet. No matter what the circumstances, an attorney can help with legal matters. I found this out the hard way and want to make sure that others know what their rights are so it doesn’t happen to them, too.

attorneys.practice_type: Personal Injury Lawyers in Phoenix, AZ
attorneys.bio:
Joel Fugate is an attorney at Phillips Law Group. He is a passionate lawyer known for his commitment to helping individuals navigate the complexities of personal injury law. Long before his time with our firm, Joel sought a career that would allow him to problem-solve while making a tangible difference in his community. The law appealed to him for its diversity and opportunities to engage and build relationships with clients from all walks of life.

Before embarking on a legal career, Joel completed his undergraduate studies at the University of Tennessee, obtaining a B.S. in Civil Engineering. He not only excelled academically but also developed decisive leadership skills as the President of the Men’s Rugby Team. Joel went on to earn his Juris Doctor from the Sandra Day O’Connor College of Law at Arizona State University. A few of Joel’s notable awards and accolades during his time at ASU include a Certificate in Law, Science and Technology and a CALI Award for Academic Excellence.

Throughout his legal career, Joel has represented both plaintiffs and defendants in all stages of the legal process – from pre-litigation, to jury trials, to appeals, and more. He has worked with countless individuals, small businesses, and Fortune 500 companies. Joel is well-versed in the art of understanding all aspects of a case and has mastered the ability to achieve results, regardless of the situation.

Joel’s work focuses on a wide range of accident, injury, sexual assault, and wrongful death cases. His true passion lies in cases that demand scientific or technical expertise, and he thrives when immersed in the intricacies of a truly complex case. He is inspired by the ability of personal injury attorneys to help people get on the right path — physically, mentally, and financially — after what is often the worst thing that has ever happened to them.

With a unique blend of legal expertise and a genuine desire to positively impact people’s lives, Joel has become a formidable force in the legal field and the courtroom. He cherishes the collaborative spirit of standing “in it to win it” with his clients, a quality that is crucial to his work with the team at Phillips Law Group.

When he is not poring over legal documents or commanding the attention of a courtroom, Joel is an avid outdoorsman, scuba diver, and world traveler. In his free time, he enjoys playing the guitar, attending concerts, eating at hidden culinary gems, and spending time with his wife and son and their rescue dog, Harlie.

Contact Joel today to discuss your legal needs and receive personalized attention from an experienced and compassionate attorney.

attorneys.practice_type: Class Actions -- Plaintiff Lawyers in Peoria, AZ
attorneys.bio:
Phoenix Personal Injury Attorney – Arizona FELA Lawyer

Kevin Michael Garrison is the past president of the Arizona Trial Lawyers-Phoenix Chapter. Kevin is a graduate of the University of Arizona College of Law and the Arizona Trial College. He has taught legal courses at Phoenix Community College, Rio Salado Community College and the Academy of Business College. He is also a member of the American Association of Justice.

After practicing in Phoenix for several years Kevin started his own firm in 1994. Dedicated to representing people who are injured and fighting for their rights. Kevin has successfully represented over 1,200 clients in all aspects of injury law in Arizona.

Railroad Injury Law - Federal Employer's Liability Act

Railroad workers are not covered by state workers' compensation laws. Railroad workers are covered by the Federal Employer's Liability Act (FELA), which was passed by Congress in 1908. Under the FELA, railroad workers can make injury claims against their railroad employers for both specific injuries and for occupational injuries, which can include:

Rotator cuff and shoulder injuries

Injuries to the knees, hips, legs, ankles and feet

Back and neck injuries

Lung injuries from dust exposure, including asbestosis, mesothelioma cancer and pneumoconiosis

Cubical tunnel syndrome

Carpal tunnel syndrome?

Injuries from inhaling toxic chemicals like solvents and welding fumes

Cumulative traumatic injuries

Under the FELA, the injured railroad worker has the right to recover the following damages:

Medical bills not paid by the railroad or the railroad's health insurance

Future medical bills and expenses

Past and future lost wages

Past and future pain and suffering

Past and future loss of enjoyment of life

Kevin Garrison represents railroad workers in FELA claims throughout the Southwest. If you are a railroad worker who has been injured on the job, you cannot fight large railroad companies like Union Pacific, Burlington Northern Santa Fe, CSX Transportation, and Norfolk Southern on your own. You need the help and expertise of a FELA attorney. It has been our experience that once a railroad worker has been injured on the job, he or she is often hounded by the railroad claim agent to give statements and to quickly settle the case. However, once you have retained the services of an attorney, then the railroad claims agent cannot talk to you about your claim, he must speak with your attorney. If you have been injured on the job as a rail road employee, let an experienced FELA attorney negotiate your case with the railroad claims department. Also, if you cannot return to work at the railroad, we can help you file for your Railroad Retirement Board sickness and disability benefits.

If you think you have been injured on the job at the railroad, contact Kevin Garrison at kevingarrison@inficad.com or call (623) 915-1100 or toll-free (877) 915-1100.

The Garrison Law Firm P.L.C., provides legal representation for railroad workers and their families throughout Arizona, California, New Mexico, Nevada, Utah, and Colorado. Including the communities of Phoenix, San Diego CA, Denver, Aurora CO, Salt Lake City, Los Angeles, Colorado Springs, Flagstaff, Santa Fe, Las Cruces, El Paso, Albuquerque, Tucson, Yuma, Provo, Ogden, Las Vegas, Reno, and Carson City NV , Williams AZ, Snowflake, Winslow, Kingman, Casa Grande, Benson, Wilcox, Cochise, Gila Bend, Welton, Greely CO, Almagordo NM, Deming NM, Grand Junction CO, Elko, Winnemucca, Sparks, Wells, Bakersfield, Glenwood, Riverside, Barstow CA.

attorneys.name: Jason D. Gellman
attorneys.practice_type: Energy and Power Infrastructure Lawyers in Phoenix, AZ
attorneys.bio:
Jason Gellman’s practice primarily focuses on public utilities, energy, telecommunications, water and administrative law. He regularly appears before the Arizona Corporation Commission on matters involving public utilities including rate cases, financings, service-area extensions and rulemakings. Additionally, he works with utilities developing renewable energy and energy efficiency implementation plans and programs. He has also appeared before the Arizona Power Plant and Transmission Line Siting Committee regarding the locating and permitting of power lines and power generation plants.

Prior to joining Roshka, DeWulf & Patten, Jason served as an attorney and senior staff counsel with the Arizona Corporation Commission from 2001 to 2006. Before that, he was a deputy county attorney with the Maricopa County Attorney’s Office from 1998 to 2001, where he regularly appeared before several courts in Maricopa County.

attorneys.name: Steven J. German
attorneys.practice_type: Bad Faith Insurance Law - Long Term Disability (Professionals) Lawyers in Phoenix, AZ
attorneys.bio:
Steve started his career at a large downtown law firm in Phoenix, Arizona, and enjoyed excellent litigation training and insight into how insurance companies and other large corporations operate and defend against lawsuits alleging bad-faith and other claims of wrongdoing. His passion, however, has always been protecting individual rights, and in 1999 he started his own law firm doing just that. By 2003, he and Danny Adelman joined forces and formed Adelman German – A Law Firm, and ever since they have been fighting tirelessly for those who are the most vulnerable.

Steve devotes his entire practice to representing people who are typically at the lowest point in their life. He treats each client individually and ensures their unique needs are met, and encourages each of them to not give up hope or feel like they are fighting alone. Steve’s goal is to embolden his clients, and prove to them that their lives are not over, that they can overcome their difficulties, and that there are people who care and will fight to give them every opportunity to recover. Going against insurance companies that are worth billions and have all the resources available to them, requires drive, skill and tenacity. Insurance companies hold all the cards, and often prey on those most vulnerable to boost their profits.

Steve and his firm’s greatest joys come after seeing a client overcome feelings of defeat, and the confidence that is instilled knowing they stood up against a powerful insurance company and won what they are rightfully owed.

Steve and his law firm’s practice is not only devoted to victims of insurance wrongdoings, but also to individuals and surviving families of catastrophic accidents, including car, truck, motorcycle, and SUV rollover and tread-separation accidents. He and his law firm have successfully litigated and taken many cases to trial in insurance bad faith lawsuits, and cases involving birth-injury, medical and podiatry malpractice, nursing home neglect, and other tort-related cases. He has recovered tens of millions against disability insurance companies with many multi-million settlements and verdicts, including a recent jury verdict of over $6.5 Million in September 2017.

His law firm offers free consultations to others victimized by insurance bad-faith practices, birth-injury and catastrophic personal injury and accident matters. Steve can be reached at steve@adelmangerman.com or on his direct line at 480-626-2700.

attorneys.name: Michael E. Gerity
attorneys.practice_type: Business and Commercial Law Lawyers in Phoenix, AZ
attorneys.bio:
Mr. Gerity has been admitted to practice law in Arizona State and Federal courts since graduating from the Arizona State University College of Law in 1994. He also is admitted to practice law in Colorado and before the United States Patent and Trademark office. Prior to forming Israel & Gerity, Mr. Gerity clerked for the chief judge of the Arizona court of appeals, served as a deputy public defender, where he received extensive trial experience, and worked for several years at a large civil litigation law firm in phoenix. He then struck out to form his own firm, and also served as of counsel to a prestigious, boutique commercial litigation firm. In law school, Mr. Gerity "wrote on" as an associate note and comment editor for the Arizona State Law Journal, received honors in legal research and writing, and was awarded best appellate brief. Mr. Gerity received his Bachelor of Science degree from Colorado State University in 1990.

Mr. Gerity has taught classes and given presentations on a wide variety of topics, including teaching at a national paralegal college and teaching a series of courses to management personnel at a top-twenty employer in the phoenix area. He has handled over thirty trials and numerous appeals before the Arizona court of appeals, the Arizona Supreme Court, and the U.S. Court of Appeals for the Federal Circuit. Mr. Gerity's practice areas include general civil litigation and commercial litigation, intellectual property and business matters, bankruptcy, trusts and estate planning, and general business representation.

When he is not working, Mr. Gerity spends time with his family, and in his "free time" he volunteers for the phoenix fire department as a licensed EMT and sings in a rock cover band.

attorneys.name: John T. Gilbert
attorneys.practice_type: Real Estate Transactions Lawyers in Scottsdale, AZ
attorneys.bio:
John Gilbert's practice focuses on commercial litigation, business and real estate law and business acquisitions. He has decades of experience in negotiating complex transactions, contracts and leases, especially in the field of real estate. He has represented clients from every area of the real estate market, including owners, developers, general contractors, and bankers.

John is an "AV" rated attorney under Martindale-Hubbell's peer review process. He previously was active in the Maricopa County Bar Association's Continuing Legal Education Committee, which he chaired in the late 1980s. He also was a co-editor of the Arizona Litigation Guide, Second Edition, published in 1993. He is a member of the State Bar of Arizona, the Maricopa County Bar Association, the Scottsdale Bar Association and the American Bar Association. He is a member of Arizona's Finest Lawyers (Sustaining Member) and was designated as Lawyer of the Month by Attorney at Law magazine in 2013 appearing on its cover. In 2015, John was named a Southwest Super Lawyer. John is admitted to practice in the state courts of Arizona and in the United States District Court of Arizona.

John was born and raised in Chicago, Illinois. He earned a B.A. in psychology from Northwestern University in Evanston, Illinois. He received his Juris Doctor degree from the Northwestern University School of Law in Chicago in 1976. Immediately following his graduation from law school, he clerked for the Honorable Jack D.H. Hays of the Arizona Supreme Court, after which he entered private practice.

Throughout his career, John has also been actively involved in the community. He has served for over ten years on the Board of Management of the Chris-Town YMCA.

attorneys.name: Donato Giovanatto
attorneys.practice_type: Personal Injury Lawyers in Phoenix, AZ
attorneys.bio:
Donato Giovanatto is a personal injury attorney at Phillips Law Group.

Donato is a native of Arizona growing up in Scottsdale. He received his Bachelor’s degree from San Jose State University and his law degree from California Western School of Law.

Since a young age, Donato has known the value of hard work and dedication, and this has never left him. His determination brought him both success in the classroom and on the field, allowing him to play professional baseball for the Los Angeles Angels Organization. This same determination is what Donato now puts into representing you.

After graduating from law school, he worked for the Arizona Attorney General’s office where he gained valuable courtroom experience and litigated countless cases. Subsequently, he was a managing attorney at another local personal injury firm before joining Phillips Law.

Donato is highly skilled in handling serious injury cases, has settled millions for his clients, and is a skillful negotiator. Donato understands that your injuries have truly affected your life, and will make sure that your voice is heard. Donato will assure, to the very best of his ability, that you are properly treated and fully compensated.

In his free time, Donato enjoys hacking it up on the golf course, attending sporting events, and spending time with his beautiful wife who is also an attorney, and their Goldendoodle, Fonzie.

Donato’s “Why”

Being attorney was a lifelong pursuit of mine that has ultimately enriched my life both professionally and personally. Growing up I have always been competitive and after my professional baseball career ended I needed a new competitive outlet. Fortunately, the legal profession filled that void and it has been both challenging and rewarding. Becoming an attorney has afforded me the opportunity to advocate for others who are facing difficult times in their lives.

attorneys.name: Allen David Glazer
attorneys.practice_type: Family Law Lawyers in Goodyear, AZ
attorneys.bio:
Allen Glazer is a dedicated professional with a diverse background in law, business, and community service, Allen brings a wealth of experience and a passion for service to every endeavor. Allen began his academic journey at California State University, Northridge, where he swam competitively as part of a program that earned numerous Division II National swim titles. He went on to earn his Juris Doctor from Loyola Law School.

Before practicing law, he founded and successfully operated a computer consulting company, earning the prestigious Small Business of the Year award from the United Chambers of Commerce—an organization representing 13 chambers across the Los Angeles area.

A committed civic leader, Allen served as both President and Treasurer of the Chatsworth/Porter Ranch Chamber of Commerce. He was also elected to multiple two-year terms on the City of Los Angeles Neighborhood Empowerment – Chatsworth Neighborhood Council, where he held key leadership roles including Vice President of the Formation Committee and Treasurer.

In his legal career, Allen has focused primarily on family law. He founded his own law practice and has been recognized for his commitment to pro bono service, receiving the Wiley W. Manuel Pro Bono Services Certificate for providing over 50 hours of free legal assistance in one year through the Harriett Buhai Center for Family Law. He also volunteered with the Los Angeles County Bar Association’s Domestic Violence Project, helping survivors navigate the legal system during times of crisis.

Currently he resides in Buckeye, Arizona with his wife. Allen also shares his home with a German Shepherd/Husky mix, a Golden Retriever, and a rabbit. He is a proud father of two sons. An avid enthusiast of golf, car racing, and cycling, one of his most memorable adventures was riding his bicycle from Disneyland in California to Disney World in Florida.

attorneys.name: Alejandro Gonzales
attorneys.practice_type: General Business Lawyers in Tucson, AZ
attorneys.bio:
Alejandro was born and raised in Nogales, Arizona and considers himself an Arizonan through and through – he is a fan of the Arizona Cardinals, Arizona Diamondbacks, Phoenix Suns, and University of Arizona athletics.

Alejandro enlisted in the United States Marine Corps shortly after September 11, 2001. In addition to being a combat veteran, Alejandro deployed to the Indian Ocean and was awarded with the Navy’s Humanitarian Medal for his efforts in Operation Unified Assistance following the aftermath of the catastrophic Indian Ocean earthquake that devastated and displaced many in Indonesia. After completing his enlistment, Alejandro served as a deputy sheriff in Southern Arizona for eight-years.

Alejandro received his undergraduate degree from the University of Arizona and attended Marquette Law School in Milwaukee, Wisconsin, where he was the Co-President of the Hispanic and Latino Law Student Association and a public interest law scholar.

Alejandro began his legal career serving as a prosecutor for the same county in which he served as a deputy sheriff. Alejandro joins Goldberg and Osborne after practicing general business and real estate law with the law firm of Thompson Krone in Tucson, Arizona.

In his spare time, Alejandro enjoys playing basketball, watching sports, riding his motorcycle, and spending time with his family, particularly with his niece and nephew.

Alejandro reads, writes, and speaks Spanish fluently.

attorneys.name: Elizabeth Gonzalez Esq.
attorneys.practice_type: Car Accidents Lawyers in Glendale, AZ
attorneys.bio:
Serious Injury Lawyer Elizabeth “Liz” Gonzalez, Esq., is a Partner at Accident Justice. Liz plays a very important role on the firm’s litigation team. Liz is a trial attorney at heart, with over a dozen jury trials and twenty bench trials under her belt, giving her extensive experience in the courtroom.

Liz knows the difference between being victorious at trial or not, and it begins well before she enters the courtroom. She spends a vast amount of time reviewing her clients’ cases and strategizing a customized plan for their own unique situations. Liz also takes great pride in counseling her clients through the stages of their case, preparing them for the litigation process and advocating on their behalf. If insurance companies refuse to fully compensate her clients, she will not shy away from the courtroom.

Liz has a Bachelor’s Degree in Communications from California State Polytechnic University, Pomona, California, where she made the Dean’s list and competed with the Mock Trial Team, winning multiple awards. Liz then continued to the Phoenix School of Law to pursue her Juris Doctorate degree. In law school, she not only earned a position on the Law Review, but she also competed on the Moot Court Team with Managing Attorney, Abdul Jaiteh, Esq.

Prior to joining Accident Justice in 2018, Liz was a public defender in Mohave County, where she defended and protected the rights of thousands of individuals charged with misdemeanor and serious felony matters. Liz then moved to a private firm, where she continued representing those with criminal matters, as well as family or domestic cases and personal injury cases. While Liz has shifted from criminal defense to civil practice, she fully understands what it means to fight and advocate for those who are up against all odds and have everything to lose.

attorneys.name: Craig Gordon
attorneys.practice_type: Lawyers in Tucson, AZ
attorneys.bio:
Craig practiced elder law with the firm from 1985 through 2008. He had extensive experience in Medicaid/ALTCS planning, including Special Needs Trusts, was certified as a Specialist in Estate and Trust Law by the State Bar of Arizona, and recognized as a Certified Elder Law Attorney (CELA) by the National Elder Law Foundation (NELF). Craig was also selected as a Fellow of the National Academy of Elder Law Attorneys (NAELA) in 1995 and Best Lawyers in America in 2007.

Craig has been quite active serving on the Boards and Executive Committees of both national and statewide elder law organizations (NAELA, NELF, Az-NAELA, Senior Rights PAC), while always looking out for the best interests of his clients. Craig has lived in Tucson since 1976 and is married to Barbara Smith, a pediatrician, and they have two daughters. Craig enjoys bicycling, birding, and SCUBA diving. Craig retired from the practice of law for health reasons in 2008.

attorneys.name: Tracy Gordon
attorneys.practice_type: Family Law Lawyers in Phoenix, AZ
attorneys.bio:
Tracy Gordon is a partner at Schmidt McElwee & Gordon, PLLC. Working out of the firm's offices in Phoenix, Arizona, she focuses her practice exclusively on family law matters, and she represents clients in Maricopa County and throughout the state.

Ms. Gordon attended Arizona State University in Tempe as an undergraduate, and she majored in finance and received a Bachelor of Science. She then joined an area family law firm, and she served as a paralegal for several years before deciding that she wanted to pursue a legal education. Ms. Gordon thereupon enrolled at what was then known as the Phoenix School of Law and which subsequently changed its name to Arizona Summit Law School. While she was there, she was a member of the Phoenix Law Review, and she served a legal writing clerkship at The Judicial Branch of Arizona in Maricopa County. This latter experience helped to give Ms. Gordon a strong background in civil litigation matters which she uses today in her practice.

Ms. Gordon was awarded her Juris Doctor in 2011, and she was admitted to practice before all Arizona state courts later that year. She has been with her current firm since that time, handling a wide variety of family law cases. Many of Ms. Gordon's clients are facing the end of their marriages, and she helps them with the related divorce legal issues of parenting time, child support, spousal maintenance, and the division of complex assets, the latter in which her finance background is an advantage for her clients when it comes to valuations. Other matters that Ms. Gordon has worked on have included the preparation and review of prenuptial and post-marital agreements.

attorneys.name: Matthew H. Green
attorneys.practice_type: Immigration Lawyers in Tucson, AZ
attorneys.bio:
The Law Offices of Matthew H. Green focuses on the aggressive defense of immigrants. A native of Arizona, Mr. Green understands the difficulties that immigrants and families of immigrants face when a loved one is charged with a crime. He knows how frightening it can be for someone who has been arrested by the Immigration and Customs Enforcement Agency ("ICE"), and placed into removal, or deportation, proceedings. Often times, an immigrant faces deportation only after he is found guilty of committing a crime. For this reason, Mr. Green’s law practice focuses on effective criminal defense of immigrants charged with crimes so that they may avoid removal (deportation) charges altogether.

In addition to criminal defense, Mr. Green's law firm also emphasizes removal (deportation) defense of those immigrants who must fight deportation. The majority of Mr. Green's clients are placed in detention in Florence, Arizona, or Eloy, Arizona. Our law firm represents these individuals in the Eloy and Florence Immigration Courts. Mr. Green represents immigrants with cases in the Tucson Immigration Court, and the law firm serves those people who are arrested in Nogales, Arizona, and Douglas, Arizona.

Mr. Green also represents clients charged with felonies in the U.S. District Court in Tucson, Arizona. At any given time, Mr. Green defends a variety of clients who have been charged with crimes like Illegal Reentry, Alien Smuggling or Transportation, and Transportation of Drugs. The majority of these clients are undocumented immigrants. In the United States of America, even undocumented immigrants enjoy the same rights as U.S. citizens. Mr. Green fights to protect his clients' rights, in their criminal cases and in their immigration cases.

For those immigrants who have been living in Arizona or other parts of the United States, the Law Offices of Matthew H. Green helps these people and their families gain legal immigration status. If you are an undocumented immigrant with family members who are United States citizens, or even Legal Permanent Residents, then we may be able to help you obtain a visa or a "green card." At the Law Offices of Matthew H. Green, our staff will help you identify all possible alternatives for legally coming to, and remaining in, the United States of America.

Mr. Green and his staff are fluent in Spanish. The majority of our immigration clients speak Spanish, and we are happy to answer questions from Spanish-speaking clients and their family members.

She has a passion for dance, art, travel, reading, writing, and anything outdoors.

attorneys.name: Theron M. Hall Jr.
attorneys.practice_type: Estate Planning Lawyers in Mesa, AZ
attorneys.bio:
Theron M Hall, Jr. (aka Tim) learned early in life the need of proper management of estates for their preservation. Born and raised in Apache County, Arizona, Tim worked for his parents' title company as a youth, where he gained a lasting appreciation for those who work hard to acquire their estates. Now, as an estate planning attorney, protecting his clients' future through quality legal service has become his hallmark.

After graduating cum laude with a Bachelor of Arts degree in English and a Master's degree in Public Administration from Brigham Young University, Tim earned his Juris Doctor degree from the University of Chicago. During his legal studies, he was employed as a research associate with the American Bar Foundation. He is currently a member of the State Bar of Arizona and the Iowa State Bar Association.

During his four years as an officer in the Judge Advocate General Corps of the U.S. Navy, Tim gained extensive criminal trial experience and began preparing trusts and other estate planning documents for servicemen. When he returned to Arizona to practice, he continued his emphasis on helping clients preserve their assets.

Tim provides a high level of skill and knowledge to planning for those of high net worth with complex estates. A complex estate requires advance forms of estate planning such as LLCs, FLLPs, ILITs, QPRTs, GRATs and more.

Advanced estate planning helps individuals and families of considerable wealth to detour unnecessary taxes that can drastically reduce their estate. These estates are affected by a combination of at least four taxes: Estate tax, Generation-skipping transfer tax, Gift tax and income tax. Tim helps these clients take advantage of lifetime leveraging with advanced estate planning tools, thereby reducing the tax costs to the estate.

Advances estate planning incorporates business succession planning strategies to help you ensure your business is preserved both during your life and thereafter. Tim Hall has helped families with humble or substantial estates to protect their assets, businesses and their legacy for their loved ones.

Tim is a member of the American Academy of Estate Planning Attorneys (AAEPA). Acknowledged by his peers with the highest rating an attorney can earn, Tim received an AV peer-review rating from Martindale-Hubbell.
