attorneys.name: Michael A. Halliday
attorneys.practice_type: Estate Planning Lawyers in Mesa, AZ
attorneys.bio:
Michael Halliday was born and raised in Mesa, AZ. He is the youngest of 4 children. Michael learned early on the importance of establishing a proper estate plan. He witnessed firsthand his mom and aunts fighting over his grandmother's meager estate, causing a rift in their relationship that would last until his aunts died. This experience shaped Michael's focus to ensure individuals and families could avoid this unnecessary trauma and have peace of mind by establishing and maintaining a suitable estate plan.

Experience

Michael attended Mesa Community College earning an Associates of Arts degree and then graduated from Arizona State University, Cum Laude with a Bachelor of Arts degree in Chinese. During his time at ASU, he participated in a 9-week Chinese language immersion program at the Peoples University in Beijing China. After graduation, he attended Willamette University, College of Law and in 2004. After his first year in law school, he attended a 5-week International Law program at the East China University of Political Science and Law in Shanghai, China.

Professional Experience

He worked at a small firm out of law school. It was at this law firm that he learned the vital significance of proper planning for individuals and families. This experience ultimately set the stage to open his own firm a few years later and focus primarily on estate planning, guardianships and conservatorships, and trust/probate administration.

He joined the Morris Hall team in 2018 and instantly felt a sense of comradery and purpose. He has experienced first-hand how Morris Hall gives back to the community through seminars, question and answer series, participation in charitable events (Phoenix Children's Hospital - Ignite Hope; St. Mary's Food Bank and Feed My Starving Children - food packing), and generous charitable donations.

He is a member of the American Academy of Estate Planning Attorneys and is a member of the State Bar of Arizona and Oregon. While in Oregon, Michael sat on the Board of Directors for five years for the Willamette Heritage Center (formerly Mission Mill Museum), a non-profit organization whose aim is to preserve historical buildings and artifacts for the education and benefit of the local community. Since moving to Arizona, Michael volunteers with the Arizona Animal Welfare League ("AAWL") providing free pet trust seminars.

Personal

Michael is married to his high school sweetheart, Amy Jo and they have 4 beautiful and healthy children and a rescue dachshund named Noodles. He enjoys basketball, golf and hiking with his wife and kids. Not only has Michael served many clients over the last 16 years as an attorney, but he has spent thousands of hours as a volunteer coach (including basketball, baseball, soccer, and volleyball), as a leader in the Boy Scouts of America, as well as various positions for his church.

attorneys.name: Myles P. Hassett
attorneys.practice_type: Mediation Lawyers in Phoenix, AZ
attorneys.bio:
Born in Ireland, Myles Patrick Hassett grew up in a country mired in a violent, centuries-old sectarian conflict that cried out for reconciliation between the warring factions. When the conflict was finally resolved in 1998—with U.S. Senator George Mitchell as mediator—Myles was inspired to focus on mediation as way to successfully end litigation. Drawing on his unique experience, Myles says: “In over 30 years practicing law, I've learned there is no compromise of principle in the peaceful resolution of differences, only the knowledge that not all battles need be fought to a bitter end, and the hope that people can reconcile and rise above whatever conflict brought them to my door."

Having been admitted to practice in Ireland in 1988, Myles moved to the United States, where he is first Irish solicitor licensed in both Arizona and California. Myles is also the founder of Acordia Dispute Resolution, a mediation/arbitration practice, and is a well-known author and speaker on insurance and dispute resolution issues. As your mediator, Myles is dedicated to applying principles of “Win-Win Resolution” to settle your case. See more at www.acordia-adr.com

Throughout his decades-long litigation career, Myles has served as a neutral in hundreds of cases. This includes serving as a Judge pro tem for the Arizona Superior Court (Maricopa County) as a court-appointed arbitrator and settlement judge, as well as in his capacity as a private mediator. Myles adds: “Whether your case involves insurance, personal injury, wrongful death, commercial or professional liability issues, I believe I have the necessary skillset and experience to get it resolved.”

Myles has been awarded Martindale Hubbell’s highest peer-reviewed “AV” designation and is listed in Southwest Super Lawyers. In recognition for his decades of work as a trial advocate, Myles was elected as a member of the International Society of Barristers in 2020. He is also a member of the Arizona Chapter of the National Academy of Distinguished Neutrals.

In addition to his dispute resolution practice, Myles is passionate about Irish history, photography, and celebrating St. Patrick’s Day.

sections.title: Overview
sections.content:
Mr. Hildebrand, an experienced Arizona divorce lawyer, has established a well respected reputation for providing results in Arizona divorce matters. Mr. Hildebrand meticulously applies his extensive knowledge and understanding of Arizona divorce laws to achieve practical solutions for his clients in their family law matters. As a distinguished Arizona divorce lawyer, Mr. Hildebrand has passionately advocated on behalf of his clients in courtrooms throughout the state of Arizona for over a decade.

Mr. Hildebrand is regarded by other Arizona divorce lawyers as a highly knowledgeable and skilled negotiator and advocate for his clients' interests. Mr. Hildebrand's extensive experience is regularly relied upon by other Arizona divorce lawyers as a mediator to negotiate divorce settlements for their clients' cases and to represent their own family members in divorce related matters.

Arizona divorce matters are highly stressful. That stress, however, will be significantly mitigated by knowing that your Arizona divorce case is being managed by a dedicated team of experienced and knowledgeable Arizona divorce professionals. Hildebrand Law, P.C. is one of Maricopa County and Arizona's preeminent divorce law firms. The law firm is dedicated solely to the practice of Arizona divorce cases. Focusing only upon Arizona divorce matters allow the professionals at Hildebrand Law, P.C. to remain current on the constantly changing Arizona divorce laws.

The professionals at Hildebrand Law, P.C. focus upon providing practical and effective solutions for all of our Arizona divorce clients. If you are facing the reality of a divorce in Arizona, you deserve the peace of mind that comes with knowing your most precious assets are being guarded by a committed team who focus only upon Arizona divorce cases.

Mr. Hildebrand's practice covers all areas of Arizona family law including divorce, legal separation, paternity, spousal maintenance, community property division, business appraisals incident to a divorce, child custody, child abuse, child support, and orders of protection.

The experienced, knowledgeable, and dedicated legal professionals at Hildebrand Law, P.C. are committed to exceeding every client's expectations by providing the highest quality legal services, advice and representation in Arizona divorce matters. If you are in need of representation for a divorce matter, put the resources of an experienced, respected and qualified Arizona divorce lawyer to work for you by contacting Hildebrand Law, P.C. today.

Mr. Hildebrand is regarded amongst colleagues as a highly knowledgeable and skilled negotiator and advocate for his clients' interests. With his extensive experience and reputation, Mr. Hildebrand has earned the respect of other attorneys, experts and judges with whom he has practiced. He is regularly consulted by other attorneys in the community, who leverage his knowledge and experience to act as a mediator to assist in resolving their own clients' legal matters. In fact, Mr. Hildebrand has been called upon by attorneys themselves to represent them and their family members in personal legal matters.

Mr. Hildebrand is licensed to practice law in the State of Arizona and the United States District Courts; is a member of the Arizona Bar Association, the Maricopa County Bar Association, the Family Law Section of the Maricopa County Bar Association, is a member of Mensa; and is a local contact counsel for the National Center for Missing and Exploited Children, supplying pro bono legal services to the U.S. State Department to secure the return of children abducted from around the world through use of the international Hague Convention Treaty.

Mr. Hildebrand graduated cum laude from Arizona State University with a Bachelor of Science degree in Finance in 1991 and received his Juris Doctorate degree from Arizona State University in 1994. While attending law school, Mr. Hildebrand worked as an intern to the recently appointed Vice Chief Justice of the Arizona Supreme Court and has been appointed as a Professor of Legal Studies at an accredited local university.

attorneys.practice_type: Lawyers in Phoenix, AZ
attorneys.bio:
Matt Hilscher stands out as a highly skilled personal injury lawyer at Esquire Law in Phoenix, Arizona. He approaches his work with a high level of empathy, which makes him a formidable litigator. Attorney Hilsher genuinely cares about his clients and is dedicated to fighting for those facing life’s most challenging situations. He is known for his unwavering commitment to his clients and is often described as relentless by those who have worked with him. Attorney Hilsher’s confidence stems from his extensive experience litigating challenging legal issues in court for almost a decade. His empathetic approach to his work allows him to connect with his clients on a deeper level, and he is always willing to go the extra mile to ensure that they receive the justice they deserve.

Originally from Fort Worth, Texas, Hilsher moved to Arizona for school and quickly fell in love with the area’s access to outdoor activities. He decided to stay in Phoenix and began his legal career as a private criminal defense attorney. Hilsher defended individuals charged with major felony cases in every court in Arizona, gaining a unique perspective on juries and trial preparation. Despite being thrown into the deep end with his first trial being for first-degree murder, Hilsher’s experience gave him the ability to pinpoint a case’s lynchpin in front of a future jury.

Matt Hilscher brings a tenacious spirit to his personal injury cases, which sets him apart from other attorneys. He approaches each case with a high level of energy and enthusiasm, and his passion for legal battles is evident in his work. Matt’s non-judgmental approach to his clients is a testament to his professionalism and dedication to his work. He strives to provide his clients with the best possible legal representation and is committed to achieving the best possible outcome for each case.

attorneys.name: Randall A. Hinsch
attorneys.practice_type: Personal Injury Lawyers in Phoenix, AZ
attorneys.bio:
Randy Hinsch was born in South Bend, Indiana. He received his Bachelor of Arts degree from Arizona State University in 1982 and graduated law school with his Juris Doctorate from Pepperdine University in 1985. Randy went to work for a small litigation firm in Phoenix, Arizona, to gain trial experience immediately while being able to provide clients the hands-on, personable representation often missing from larger firms. He joined the law firm of Plattner Verderame, P.C. in 1992, again enjoying the opportunity given in a small litigation firm to provide personal, quality representation to clients. Randy became a Partner in 2001. Randy has been licensed to practice in Arizona since 1985. He is a member of the State Bar of Arizona, the Arizona Trial Lawyers Association and the American Association for Justice. He also has licensure with the Ninth Circuit Federal Court of Appeals and the U.S. District Court, District of Arizona. His practice focus has been centered on wrongful death and personal injury and medical malpractice. Randy is a State Bar of Arizona Certified Specialist in Personal Injury and Wrongful Death Litigation. According to the State Bar of Arizona, less than 2% of lawyers in Arizona have this specialty certification. In 2011, Randy was selected as of Arizona’s Finest Lawyers. (azfinestlawyers.org).

In addition to helping clients, Randy and his wife and daughters support Friends for Life, www.azfriends.org , a no-kill shelter for dogs and cats in Gilbert, Arizona, including fostering dogs until permanent homes can be found for them.

attorneys.name: Ricky John Horton
attorneys.practice_type: Personal Injury Lawyers in Phoenix, AZ
attorneys.bio:
Rick Horton is a trial attorney at David Shapiro Law, PLLC concentrating his practice in personal injury matters. More specifically, Rick focuses on motor vehicle and trucking collisions, catastrophic injuries, wrongful death, products liability, premises liability, and civil rights violations.

"For over 25 years, Rick has litigated complex issues of liability and damages nationwide, serving as lead counsel in several high-profile, catastrophic injury cases."

Rick is licensed to practice in Arizona, Oklahoma, and Missouri, and is admitted in both state and federal courts. He received his bachelor's degree from Baylor University, where he was a member of the Baylor baseball team, and earned his Juris Doctor (J.D.) from the University of Tulsa College of Law.

After graduation, Rick defended insurance companies in auto collision cases, as well as premises liability cases, having tried over 75 cases to a jury. His superior litigation skills earned the trust of insurance companies such as Allstate, Farmers, State Farm, and Liberty Mutual. Preferring to represent individual victims as opposed to big companies, Rick now uses his experiences to fight on behalf of victims in motor vehicle collisions, products liability, premises liability, catastrophic injury, and wrongful death cases.

Along with his work as an attorney, Rick enjoys spending time with his wife, their horse, and two border collie dogs in the great outdoors of Arizona.

Awards and Honors

Honors

Martindale-Hubbell’s highest AV Preeminent rating (5.0)

attorneys.bio:
Since 2005, Chris has focused his practice primarily on employment cases. He handles a wide variety of employment cases ranging from discrimination and harassment to cases involving accommodations for individuals with disabilities, retaliation, and wage and hour cases. Chris is experienced in handling cases from their initial phases through jury verdicts.

Chris’s personal philosophy of practicing law is that he firmly believes his cases can change the world, one case at a time. Because each case is very important to him, he works to bring about a just resolution as swiftly as he can. Chris strongly believes in representing his clients ethically and with integrity.

He later worked for the Civil Rights Division of the Arizona Attorney General’s Office for over four years and the Equal Employment Opportunity Commission for more than six years.

attorneys.name: Robert C Howard Jr.
attorneys.practice_type: Divorce Lawyers in Scottsdale, AZ
attorneys.bio:
Attorneys aren't always the brunt of the joke; sometimes, they're the ones making the jokes. Case in point is attorney and stand-up comedian Robert C. Howard, Jr. (he goes by "Bob"), who won the Funniest Person in the Valley contest in 2001 and opened for Wanda Sykes at the Tempe Improv. In 2013, he won the John O'Connor Humor Competition sponsored by the Phoenix 100 Rotary Club. Through 2014, he wrote "Finding the Funny" - a monthly column for the Fountain Hills Times.

But Bob isn't all about laughs. In 2008, the State Bar of Arizona named him as one of the top 50 pro bono attorneys in the state. In 2011, he was inducted into the Scottsdale Historymakers Hall of Fame by the Scottsdale Chamber of Commerce.

He served as President of the Scottsdale Bar Association from 1985-1986 and, in 2006, the Association gave him the Award of Excellence for Community Service. The Maricopa County Bar gave him the Volunteer of the Year Award in 2000 and the Longevity Award for Outstanding Performance in 2014 for the time he has devoted to the Family Law Assistance Program (FLAP).

Bob promoted the idea and helped establish a monthly legal assistance program at the Paiute Neighborhood Center, where members of the Scottsdale Bar Association provide free legal services once a month. He started the annual fundraising breakfast for the Center and started a program with the Scottsdale Charros for Scottsdale School students to have lunch and a few hours at the stadium during the spring training season. He has also been on the negotiation team for the Charros which resulted in long-term contracts with the San Francisco Giants.

As if all of that weren't enough, Bob has served as President of the Scottsdale Charros, the Partners for Paiute Neighborhood Center, and the Scottsdale Education Foundation. He served a six-year term on the Scottsdale Airport Advisory Commission and acted as their Chairman for two years. He was a member of Class I of Scottsdale Leadership and later served on that Board and as President from 1992-1993. He was also honored with the Frank Hodges Leadership Award in 1999, the Charro of the Year Award in 1988, and the Charro Lifer of the Year Award in 2002.

A native of Brooklyn, New York, Bob's family moved to Arizona in 1960. He graduated from ASU with a Bachelor's Degree in Political Science and earned his Juris Doctorate in 1976 from ASU Law School. He was admitted to the Arizona Bar in 1976 and was formerly with the firm of Jekel, Howard & Thomson LLP in Scottsdale.

In his spare time, Bob likes to play poker, tennis, and slow pitch softball. He and Kathy, his wife of 23 years, love to spend weekends in their cabin in Prescott. Bob has a son, two stepsons, and five grandchildren.

attorneys.name: Daniel Hutto
attorneys.firm_name: Law Office of Daniel Hutto, PLLC
attorneys.practice_type: Criminal Law Lawyers in Phoenix, AZ
attorneys.bio:
Daniel Hutto is a native of Arizona and was born and raised in Tucson. He attended the University of Arizona where he received his B.A. in Political Science. Daniel then attended the Sandra Day O'Connor College of Law at Arizona State University where he earned his Juris Doctorate.

During law school, Daniel worked under a limited practice certification for both the Maricopa County Attorney's Office and City of Phoenix Prosecutor's Office. Following law school, Daniel accepted employment with a local civil and family law firm. During this time, he gained critical knowledge in all areas of family law including: divorce, property division, legal decision-making, parenting time, child support, and spousal maintenance.

In 2013, Daniel accepted a position as a Deputy County Attorney at the Maricopa County Attorney's Office. As a former prosecutor for MCAO, Daniel has experience handling both felony and misdemeanor offenses. Ultimately, he ascended to the Vehicular Crimes Unit, where he focused on Aggravated DUI's, Aggravated Assaults, Endangerment and other vehicle based offenses. This experience gives him a unique understanding of the criminal justice system, giving him an advantage in negotiating a plea and preparing for trial.

Daniel is a member of both the Maricopa County Bar Association and American Bar Association.

attorneys.name: Kyle A. Israel
attorneys.practice_type: Construction Law Lawyers in Phoenix, AZ
attorneys.bio:
Kyle A. Israel practices extensively litigation in the areas of personal injury, construction, commercial and general liability. He has written and lectured extensively on construction law issues. He has argued the landmark Arizona construction defect case Lofts at Fillmore v. Reliance before the Arizona Supreme Court. He was the founding Chair of the Construction Law Section of the Maricopa Bar. Kyle regularly conducts negligence, construction, and insurance seminars.

Kyle was admitted to practice law in Arizona State and Federal courts since graduating from the Arizona State University College of Law ("ASU") in 1994. At ASU, Kyle received the US Law Award for Academic Excellence. He was named Outstanding Advocate. He represented the ASU Moot Court team in the finals of the National Trial Advocacy Championships in Chicago, Illinois.

After working for several years for a large insurance defense firm, Kyle founder Israel & Gerity, PLLC in 2002, where he has headed up the firm’s litigation practice ever since.

In the area of personal injury, Kyle has handled many serious injury cases arising in the areas of auto, construction, medical malpractice, dram shop, animal attacks and more. Kyle has received favorable verdicts and settlements in each of these areas.

In the area of construction litigation, Kyle has represented owners, contractors, property managers and design professionals. In commercial litigation, he has represented business owners, art dealers, real estate developers, title insurers, liability insurers, etc.

Kyle has tried many cases to verdict, receiving nearly 100% favorable verdicts.

Kyle serves as arbitrator, umpire and mediator in various civil litigation and insurance disputes.

Recently, Kyle was anonymously selected by his peers as a member of the initial class of Arizona’s Finest Lawyers, http://www.azfinestlawyers.org/, an organization that seeks to elevate the practice of law and that selected the top 2% of Arizona attorneys meeting their criteria.

attorneys.name: David Iversen
attorneys.practice_type: Personal Injury - Plaintiff Lawyers in Phoenix, AZ
attorneys.bio:
David joined the Kelly Law Team after serving as a Partner at Hacker Murphy, LLP, where he adeptly managed a demanding caseload of over 100 litigation and trial-ready cases. He has first-chaired more than a dozen jury trials and consistently achieved outstanding results in mediations and arbitrations, securing favorable resolutions for his clients. Among his notable accomplishments is a $9.5 million settlement in a complex motor carrier crash involving 18 estates and billion-dollar corporations—the highest settlement in that county’s history.

David's expertise encompasses catastrophic injury litigation, wrongful death, medical malpractice, and class actions. His unwavering dedication to legal excellence has earned him industry recognition, including being named a Super Lawyers “Rising Star” (2017-2025) and a Best Lawyers “Ones to Watch” (2021-2025) for personal injury, medical malpractice, products liability, and commercial litigation.

Beyond the courtroom, David is committed to mentoring young attorneys and advancing legal education. He has led law clerk programs, overseen new litigation associates, and actively participated in professional and charitable organizations. He serves as a Board Member for the Capital District Trial Lawyers Association, Albany County Bar Foundation, and the American Cancer Society of the Capital Region.

David earned his Juris Doctor from Albany Law School and his Bachelor of Arts from the State University of New York at Albany. Licensed to practice in Arizona and New York, he brings a wealth of litigation experience, a strategic mindset, and a relentless pursuit of justice to the Kelly Law Team’s growing Litigation Department.

We are proud to have David as part of our team. His trial advocacy skills and client-first approach will continue to drive success for our firm and the individuals we serve.

How do I choose a lawyer?
Comfort Level – Are you comfortable telling the lawyer personal information? Does the lawyer seem interested in solving your problem?
Credentials – How long has the lawyer been in practice? Has the lawyer worked on other cases similar to yours?
Cost – How are the lawyer's fees structured — hourly or flat fee? Can the lawyer estimate the cost of your case?
City – Is the lawyer's office conveniently located?
Not sure what questions to ask a lawyer?
Here are a few to get you started:
How long have you been in practice?
How many cases like mine have you handled?
How often do you settle cases out of court?
What are your fees and costs?

It is always a good idea to research your lawyer prior to hiring. Every state has a disciplinary organization that monitors attorneys, their licenses, and consumer complaints. By researching lawyer discipline you can:
Ensure the attorney is currently licensed to practice in your state
Gain an understanding of his or her historical disciplinary record, if any.
Determine the seriousness of complaints/issues which could range from late bar fees to more serious issues requiring disciplinary action.

attorneys.practice_type: Car Accidents Lawyers in Glendale, AZ
attorneys.bio:
With a career built on rare insider insight into the insurance industry, Abdul brings a strategic edge to every case he handles. Before becoming a plaintiff’s attorney, Abdul spent years working within the insurance world—an experience that gives him a deep understanding of how insurers evaluate, negotiate, and fight claims. How Does The Client Define Success

At Accident Justice, success is defined by the trust we earn, the standards we uphold, and the lives we help rebuild. It’s not about case counts or billboards—it’s about doing the right thing, every time. We approach every case with integrity, urgency, and purpose, driven by a shared belief that our clients deserve more than generic representation. Success means showing up fully for our clients, for our community, and for each other. It’s measured in the relief a client feels when they’re finally heard, the difference we make outside the courtroom, and the growth we achieve together. When we lead with optimism and stay committed to our values, success follows—one person, one case, one outcome at a time.

Primary Approach

At Accident Justice, our approach is rooted in delivering personalized, high-quality representation tailored to each client’s unique situation. Abdul takes great pride in having built a serious injury law practice grounded in individualized attention, not mass production. He made a deliberate decision to reject the model of a high-volume “factory law firm” that applies a one-size-fits-all strategy to thousands of cases. Instead, he has purposefully structured the firm to take on a limited number of personal injury cases, ensuring that every client receives the focused strategy, thoughtful advocacy, and compassionate care their case deserves.

Educational Work

Abdul is passionate about empowering individuals with knowledge of their legal rights. He has delivered numerous informational seminars on personal injury law, insurance issues, and legal rights at churches, nonprofit organizations, universities, and community centers. attorneys.name: Ruthann James
attorneys.practice_type: Personal Injury Lawyers in Phoenix, AZ
attorneys.bio:
Ruthann James is a Partner Attorney with Phillips Law Group. She was born and raised in New Jersey and received her undergraduate degree in Literature and Communications from Pace University, Pleasantville, NY. She then went on to earn her Juris Doctorate at Pace University School of Law, White Plains, NY.

Ruthann moved to the Phoenix area in 1993 and was admitted to the State Bar of Arizona the same year. In 1994 she joined the law firm of Goldberg & Osborne where she practiced plaintiff’s personal injury, wrongful death, and negligence law. Ruthann remained with Goldberg & Osborne as Managing Attorney until 2006.

Ruthann eventually opened her own practice where she continued to represent plaintiffs in actions involving personal injury, wrongful death, and general civil litigation. She later joined the team at Phillips Law Group on June 1, 2009, and continues to pursue justice for victims hurt as a result of another’s negligence.

Ruthann is admitted to practice before the Arizona Supreme Court and the U.S. District Court in Arizona. She is a member of the Arizona State Bar, Maricopa County Bar Association, and the Arizona Trial Lawyers Association, and was accepted as a 2016 American Institute of Personal Injury Attorneys 10 Best Female Attorney for client satisfaction.

He also participates in community outreach programs to provide resources for the deaf.

We are pleased to extend a warm welcome to him as a new member of the Accident Justice team.

attorneys.bio:
At the Law Office of Kathryn L. Johnson, PLC, my goal is to give you the personal attention and one on one counseling that you deserve in your legal matter. Every matter is important in this office.

I have been an attorney in California since 1992 and in Arizona since 1999. I am also an Arizona real estate and former mortgage broker. I grew up in Tucson, and am now faced with helping my clients here who are in a financially bad situation. Foreclosures are on the rise and real estate values have plummeted. The local job market is virtually nonexistent at the moment, and people living here in Tucson and the surrounding areas are being severely affected. People are losing their jobs, are facing foreclosure, and are being harassed and subjected to lawsuits and garnishments due to overwhelming debt.

The emphasis of my business is to provide debt relief solutions to individuals and small businesses. I can help with foreclosure, harassing creditor calls, lawsuits, garnishments and repossessions. Because of my unique background, I am able to analyze your situation from many different angles and provide you with real solutions to your problems. I am very low pressure, I offer free initial consultations, my fees are low, and I have evening and weekend appointments available to meet around your schedule if necessary. My office is conveniently located in downtown Tucson.

Help can be on the way - all you have to do is call for your free initial consultation. Please don't be embarrassed to ask for help. Call (520) 743-2257 today.

attorneys.name: Adrienne R. Jones
attorneys.practice_type: Personal Injury Lawyers in Phoenix, AZ
attorneys.bio:
Adrienne is an Arizona native, born and raised. She completed her undergraduate degree in Mathematics at Pepperdine University and returned to the Valley to teach mathematics. While teaching, she earned her Master's Degree in Business Administration with a focus in Finance at Arizona State University.

Ready for a change and a new challenge, Adrienne left teaching to pursue a law degree at the University of Denver, Sturm College of Law in Denver, Colorado. While in law school, Adrienne was a member of the Colorado Women's Bar Association, Black Law Students Association, and the Criminal Law Review. She also worked as a law clerk at Evans Case Law Firm, a civil litigation firm in Denver, Colorado. Adrienne's proudest accomplishments in law school were her accolades as a member of the Sturm College of Law National Trial Team. Adrienne's first semester in the trial program, she earned the Scholastic Achievement Award. In 2013, she and her partner won the Hoffman Cup Championship, an annual trial competition held at University of Denver. The following year, Adrienne and her teammates competed against the top 16 trial programs in the country in the Annual National Trial Competition at Baylor University and finishing third, which, at the time, was the most successful finish in the history of the Sturm College of Law Trial Advocacy program. In 2015, Adrienne graduated from law school and moved back home to Phoenix where she began her legal career in family law.

In August 2018, Adrienne joined the team at AZ Premises Law as an associate attorney representing people injured as a result of others’ carelessness. Over the past five years, Adrienne has litigated cases in the federal, state, and tribal courts and has been rated a Southwest Super Lawyers Rising Star since 2020. In January 2023, Adrienne became a partner at AZ Premises Law.

Adrienne is an active member of the Arizona legal community as a member of the Arizona Black Bar, Arizona Women Lawyers Association, and Arizona Association for Justice. She continues to work with youth in her community through her involvement in the Arizona High School Mock Trial Program and enjoys CrossFit, traveling, and trying new restaurants in her spare time.

attorneys.name: Mack T. Jones
attorneys.practice_type: Trip and Fall Accidents Lawyers in Phoenix, AZ
attorneys.bio:
For over 30 years, Mack T. Jones has been a practicing civil trial attorney in Arizona, and since the mid 1990's, Mack has been certified by the State Bar of Arizona as a Specialist in Personal Injury & Wrongful Death Litigation. After graduating from Northwestern University, in 1980 he obtained a Juris Doctor degree from the University of Arizona College of Law, where he was a writer and Notes editor on the Arizona Law Review. After law school, Mr. Jones was privileged to serve as a judicial clerk for Justice James Duke Cameron of the Arizona Supreme Court.

Since 1981, Mack has been in private practice, and he founded Bohm & Jones, P.C. in 1987. Mack’s focus is and has been representing people injured through the negligence and misconduct of others, including people hurt while on the property of others, in public transportation incidents, often involving persons with disabilities, motor vehicle collisions and through defective products. Mack’s clients have received settlements and judgments totaling millions of dollars from major corporations, governmental entities, insurance companies, and the others who have caused harm to his clients.

Recognized as an authority in Arizona on premises injury cases, he is a frequent lecturer to legal groups on Premises Injury Law and on trial practice techniques. Mr. Jones has been awarded the highest rating of “AV” by the Martindale-Hubbell peer lawyer-rating service. He is a multiple year selection as an Arizona “Super Lawyer” by Southwest Super Lawyers Magazine. This publication identifies the top 5% of attorneys in each state, as chosen by their peers and through independent research.

Mack works for the public good by promoting corporate and governmental responsibility, safe premises and products and by safeguarding the rights of individuals and their families. He uses his legal and trial skills to obtain fair settlements and just verdicts for some of the most deserving in society. Mack believes that practicing law means understanding that the lawyer’s primary role is to advise and become an advocate for the client, rather than engage in a financial transaction where profit is the controlling motivation.

Mack is admitted to practice in all Arizona state courts, the United States District Court for Arizona, and the 9th Circuit of the United States Court of Appeals.

For over 30 years, Mack T. Jones has been a practicing civil trial attorney in Arizona, and since the mid 1990's, Mack has been certified by the State Bar of Arizona as a Specialist in Personal Injury & Wrongful Death Litigation. After graduating from Northwestern University, in 1980 he obtained a Juris Doctor degree from the University of Arizona College of Law, where he was a writer and Notes editor on the Arizona Law Review. After law school, Mr. Jones was privileged to serve as a judicial clerk for Justice James Duke Cameron of the Arizona Supreme Court.

Since 1981, Mack has been in private practice, and he founded Bohm & Jones, P.C. in 1987. Mack’s focus is and has been representing people injured through the negligence and misconduct of others, including people hurt while on the property of others, in public transportation incidents, often involving persons with disabilities, motor vehicle collisions and through defective products. Mack’s clients have received settlements and judgments totaling millions of dollars from major corporations, governmental entities, insurance companies, and the others who have caused harm to his clients.

Recognized as an authority in Arizona on premises injury cases, he is a frequent lecturer to legal groups on Premises Injury Law and on trial practice techniques. Mr. Jones has been awarded the highest rating of “AV” by the Martindale-Hubbell peer lawyer-rating service. He is a multiple year selection as an Arizona “Super Lawyer” by Southwest Super Lawyers Magazine. This publication identifies the top 5% of attorneys in each state, as chosen by their peers and through independent research.

Mack works for the public good by promoting corporate and governmental responsibility, safe premises and products and by safeguarding the rights of individuals and their families. He uses his legal and trial skills to obtain fair settlements and just verdicts for some of the most deserving in society. Mack believes that practicing law means understanding that the lawyer’s primary role is to advise and become an advocate for the client, rather than engage in a financial transaction where profit is the controlling motivation.

Mack is admitted to practice in all Arizona state courts, the United States District Court for Arizona, and the 9th Circuit of the United States Court of Appeals.

attorneys.name: Paul "PJ" Judd
attorneys.practice_type: Family Law Lawyers in Phoenix, AZ
attorneys.bio:
Paul D. “PJ” Judd is a dedicated family law attorney who has practiced family law exclusively since 2019. He has handled a wide variety of cases including divorce, establishment of custody, enforcement, and modification, and is very familiar with how emotionally taxing family cases can be, even at the best of times. PJ seeks to alleviate this stress for his clients while pursuing their legal objectives and is known for his empathetic approach and exceptional communication skills.

PJ is originally from Orem, Utah, and graduated of Orem High School in 2005. He went on to earn his B.S. in Political Science with a minor in Psychology from the University of Utah, frequently making the Dean’s List. He then completed his J.D. at Arizona State University in 2016, graduating with distinction for his service contributions and ranking highly in his class.

In the office, PJ is known for being easygoing, friendly, and hardworking. His colleagues appreciate his approachable demeanor and dedication to his work. PJ excels at explaining complex legal matters in an accessible way, helping clients understand their options and the benefits and drawbacks of each choice. His hardworking nature, strong communication skills, and empathetic approach make him a standout attorney who clients trust and appreciate.

Outside of the office, PJ enjoys spending time with his wife and two children. He enjoys staying in shape by lifting, outdoor adventures, and board sports including wakeboarding, snowboarding, and skateboarding. He is a self-taught gearhead and welder, and loves all things related to off-roading, car/truck building, and fabrication.

attorneys.name: Pamela L. Judd
attorneys.practice_type: Commercial Litigation Lawyers in Phoenix, AZ
attorneys.bio:
Pamela L. Judd practices in the areas of commercial litigation, bankruptcy and securities litigation. She handles claims involving security agreements, promissory notes, leases, operating agreements, corporate formation documents, fiduciary duties, contractual obligations and other business litigation matters. She has substantial experience in obtaining the dismissal of claims asserted against clients, negotiating favorable settlements, obtaining judgments in favor of clients and avoiding the discharge of clients’ judgments and claims in bankruptcy actions.

Pamela has obtained the appointment of receivers on behalf of her clients and regularly represents and works in conjunction with court-appointed receivers. She also has experience in garnishment, preliminary injunction, temporary restraining order and contempt proceedings. She serves as local counsel for regional and national financial institutions, and she has served as a court-appointed arbitrator.

Prior to joining Roshka, DeWulf & Patten in 2009, Pamela was an associate at Lewis and Roca for seven years, where she defended class action and mass tort pharmaceutical litigation, in addition to a variety of other tort and commercial litigation matters.

attorneys.name: James A. Jutry
attorneys.practice_type: State and Federal Taxation Lawyers in Tucson, AZ
attorneys.bio: JAMES A. JUTRY, a Shareholder in the Tucson office, practices in the areas of local, state and federal taxation, business and transactional planning, corporations, partnerships, limited liability companies, estate planning, probate and charitable organizations. He has been certified by the State Bar of Arizona as a tax specialist. Mr. Jutry has assisted clients in benefit and compensation planning including designing and implementing "cafeteria" or flexible benefit plans under Internal Revenue Code Section125. He has advised organizations on obtaining and maintaining tax-exempt status under Internal Revenue Code Section 501(c), including addressing such issues as improper inurement, permitted lobbying expenditures, prohibited political activity and acquisition and disposition of charitable donations. Mr. Jutry also represents taxpayers in disputes with the audit and collection divisions of the Internal Revenue Service and the Arizona Department of Revenue and in sales and use tax controversies with the Arizona Department of Revenue and local taxing authorities. Mr. Jutry received undergraduate and Master's degrees in Accounting from the University of Arizona. Prior to attending law school, he was on the staff of the Arizona Auditor General. He graduated with distinction from the University of Arizona College of Law in 1980 and thereafter attended the University of Florida where he earned a Master of Laws in Taxation in 1981. He is a Certified Public Accountant in the State of Arizona. He is also a member of the State Bars of Arizona and Florida and is admitted to practice before the United States Tax Court.

attorneys.name: Kristen Kaffer Esq.
attorneys.firm_name: The Law Office of Kristen Kaffer, PLLC
attorneys.practice_type: Family Law Lawyers in Phoenix, AZ
attorneys.bio:
Kristen Kaffer, Esq. ​is a family law attorney practicing in Phoenix and throughout Maricopa County and Arizona. Ms. Kaffer was born and raised in South Carolina but has lived in Arizona since 2004. Kristen received her undergraduate degree from Furman University in Music and her Master's and Doctoral degrees from the University of Georgia in Music.

Kristen received her law degree from Arizona State University's Sandra Day O'Connor College of Law. During law school, Kristen developed a passion for family law on both a personal and professional level. She completed externships with the Honorable Bruce Cohen and the Maricopa County Attorney's Office. After graduating from law school, Kristen completed a fellowship with the Diane Halle Center for Family Justice and served as a bailiff for the Honorable Daniel Kiley.

Prior to forming the Law Office of Kristen Kaffer, PLLC, Kristen worked as an associate family law attorney for local family law firms. Kristen is a member of the State Bar of Arizona, the Maricopa County Bar, the Arizona Association of Family Law Attorneys and the Association of Solo Practitioners and Small Firms of Arizona. She has participated with the Lawyer Referral Service, the Hope Women's Center Family Law Clinic and the Family Law Assistance Project. Kristen earned AVVO Clients' Choice awards in 2015 and 2017. She was peer-review rated by Martindale Hubbell in 2019 and named a Rising Southwest Star by Super Lawyers in 2019, 2020 and 2021.

attorneys.name: Eugene M. Kadish
attorneys.practice_type: Business & Real Estate Law Lawyers in Phoenix, AZ
attorneys.bio:
Over the past thirty years, Gene Kadish has represented numerous individuals and businesses covering a wide range of Business and Real Estate matters. His business clients include restaurateurs, real estate investor/developers, landlords, tenants, real estate brokers, property managers, and convenience store owners. He has helped organize and form dozens of business startups, including LLC's, corporations and limited partnerships. Mindful of saving time and money for his clients, Mr. Kadish promotes resolving disputes through negotiated settlements instead of litigation.

In addition to serving his business clients, Mr. Kadish has extensive experience negotiating, documenting, and closing real estate transactions. This includes preparing purchase and sale agreements, leases, deeds, promissory notes, financing instruments, and other documents dealing with real estate matters, both simple and complex. Mr. Kadish is often called upon to counsel with fellow lawyers, escrow officers, and other real estate professionals concerning complicated real estate transactions.

Committed to community service, Mr. Kadish currently serves as a member of the Board of Directors of the non-profit Arizona Center for Law in the Public Interest, a public interest law firm, and Board Chairman of the Arizona Centennial Theatre Foundation. He has served on numerous non-profit and for profit boards including Tempe Chapter of the Salvation Army, Mill Avenue Merchants Association, Tempe Arts Center, and New Times, Inc., as well as numerous governmental and quasi-governmental boards and commissions.

Mr. Kadish is committed to providing honest and straightforward advice, legal as well as practical, concerning all types of business and real estate matters.

attorneys.name: Kate L. Kane
attorneys.practice_type: Family Law Lawyers in Chandler, AZ
attorneys.bio:
Family law matters often involve more than legal issues; they touch the most personal parts of our lives. At Donaldson Stewart, PC, I understand that these cases require more than just technical knowledge; they require empathy, strategy, and unwavering advocacy. My goal is to guide clients through challenging transitions with clarity and confidence, protecting what matters most: their family and their future.

A Career Built on Versatility and Dedication

Before joining Donaldson Stewart, PC, I gained extensive experience in diverse areas of law, including real estate litigation, civil defense, and regulatory law. I represented property owners, buyers, and investors in complex real estate disputes, served as an Assistant City Attorney for the City of Mesa, and defended Maricopa County in high-stakes civil litigation. Earlier in my career, I practiced criminal defense and personal injury law, honing my skills as a persuasive negotiator and litigator. These experiences taught me to think strategically, advocate fearlessly, and remain client-focused at every step.

A Personal Connection to Family Law

I don’t just practice family law; I understand it on a personal level. As someone who has been through divorce and is now a single mother raising two young daughters, I know firsthand the emotional and practical challenges my clients face. This experience allows me to approach each case with empathy, practical insight, and a commitment to helping my clients achieve stability and peace of mind for themselves and their children.

Mediation First. Litigation When Necessary.

I believe in resolving disputes amicably whenever possible because it often leads to better outcomes for families. However, when litigation is necessary, I am a strong and prepared advocate with years of courtroom experience. My background in complex civil litigation and motion practice ensures that I bring skill, tenacity, and thorough preparation to every case.

Whole Client Representation

At Donaldson Stewart, PC, we provide more than legal solutions. We offer a supportive partnership during one of life’s most difficult transitions. With a team known for integrity and professionalism, we work tirelessly to protect your interests and help you move forward. Ready to move forward? Schedule a consultation today and take the first step toward resolution and a fresh start.

attorneys.name: John Kelly
attorneys.practice_type: Personal Injury Lawyers in Phoenix, AZ
attorneys.bio:
Mr. Kelly is the founding member of Kelly Law Team with extensive trial and litigation experience. His practice is focused on aggressively fighting to fully compensate those who have been injured by others. Mr. Kelly is considered an excellent trial attorney who has successfully litigated several jury trials. His comfort level in front of a jury allows him to obtain outstanding results in personal injury cases. This experience is also vital to his negotiation skills because the opposing party knows that he will deliver at trial. Mr. Kelly is an expert in obtaining the most value out of settlements for his injured clients. He understands that the investigation aspect of each case is an essential key to obtaining the money needed to compensate the injured party.

Mr. Kelly started his legal career in Nebraska working for the Nebraska Attorney General. During this time he was able to work with a community of people who had been injured or wronged by a local business. Mr. Kelly was a strong advocate for the consumer and worked closely with the Attorney General to make sure that the large companies treated people with integrity and did not take advantage of them. It was during this time that Mr. Kelly was able to gain insight on what an individual faces when they have been injured or wronged by a business. Often they face difficulty navigating through the process of communicating with insurance companies, reviewing medical bills, and dealing with pain and suffering.

Mr. Kelly then accepted a position with the Douglas County Attorney's Office in Omaha, Nebraska working with several attorneys to help prosecute criminal cases. He began to take interest in the litigation aspect of the law, and also helped draft important legal amendments to the Nebraska State Constitution that protected the rights of individuals. Mr. Kelly focused on legal research and investigation skills which continue to help him in obtaining bottom line results for his clients.

Mr. Kelly was then recruited to Arizona and accepted into the Arizona's Bar after law school and began his practice at the Maricopa County Attorney's Office in Phoenix, Arizona. Mr. Kelly continued to prosecute and protect those who were victims of crimes. Mr. Kelly moved up in the ranks quickly from the preliminary bureau to the trial groups and soon was in the Major Crimes Bureau prosecuting serious felony offenders. Mr. Kelly worked side by side with the County Attorney in the Repeat Offender Program which focused on protecting those injured or victimized by the most serious offenders. Mr. Kelly conducted several jury trials during this time allowing him polish his trial skills in front of several of the best judges in the state. His time in trial in front of a jury is invaluable experience that many lawyers that are twice his age unfortunately do not have.

In 2011 Mr. Kelly went into private practice and has since defended the rights of his clients with compassion and diligence. His practice included defending those who had been wronged by the State. He is now primarily working on helping fully compensate those injured in automobile accidents, medical malpractice, trip and falls, dog bites, and work related accidents.

Mr. Kelly is an attorney who is not afraid to put in the work to get the results needed for an injured client. He understands that the physical pain is not the only aspect of being injured and that often the medical bills and loss of enjoyment can be serious debilitations for the client. Mr. Kelly will take the time to sit down with each client to listen to their individual story. Too often attorneys in larger firms only want to settle claims and move on to the next client. attorneys.name: Lisa Maxtutis Kimmel
attorneys.practice_type: Personal Injury Lawyers in Casa Grande, AZ
attorneys.bio:
Lisa Maxtutis Kimmel was born in Hartford, Connecticut. Upon graduating high school at 17 years old, Lisa was not sure whether she wanted to pursue a college education so decided to take a job with a small law firm in Hartford at the encouragement of one of her high school teachers. Lisa worked for three attorneys who eventually suggested that Lisa might want to pursue a law degree herself. Lisa attended Greater Hartford Community College and later the University of Hartford while working for the same law firm and other jobs to put herself through school. Lisa earned her bachelor of arts degree in Politics and Government in 1987, and her law degree from the University of San Diego in 1990.

While in law school Lisa worked as a summer associate at Cummings & Lockwood a large corporate firm based in Stamford, Connecticut. She was offered a position before she started her third year of law school, and began working there after graduation. However, Lisa was interested in litigation and advocacy rather than corporate representation, and accepted a position as managing attorney for White Mountain Legal Aid in Show Low, Arizona, where she represented clients in domestic relations and consumer matters. After the birth of her son, Lisa transferred to the Tucson legal aid office, where she focused primarily on domestic relations matters and legislative advocacy. Lisa participated in legislation involving domestic violence and child support, and she litigated a case on child custody jurisdiction which resulted in a published Arizona Supreme Court opinion, In re Ledet (Citation).

After nearly four years at legal aid, Lisa wanted to broaden her representation of consumers and transitioned her practice to include personal injury, nursing home negligence and abuse, insurance bad faith, sexual assault, and cases involving injuries and harm to children particularly disabled children.

During her 23 years in the practice of law, Lisa has had several jury trials involving negligent road design, nursing home abuse and financial exploitation of vulnerable adults, insurance agent negligence and insurance bad faith, medical malpractice, premises liability cases and motor vehicle personal injury cases. Lisa has settled countless cases through negotiation and mediation as well as arbitrating countless others. Lisa herself has served as an arbitrator. Lisa has handled a number of appellate cases including a nursing home published opinion from the Arizona Court of Appeals Division II, Corbett v. Manor Care.

Lisa has tried cases in Pima, Maricopa, Navajo, Apache, Santa Cruz and Cochise counties as well as in the United States District Court for the District of Arizona, has litigated in federal district court in Pennsylvania and Colorado, has handled cases in White Mountain Apache and Tohono O'odham tribal courts as well as the 9th Circuit Court of Appeals and the Arizona Supreme Court.

Lisa has given presentations at the University of Arizona and a variety of professional organizations on victims' rights, domestic violence, and nursing home abuse and neglect. Lisa has volunteered for non-profit organizations focusing on advocacy of victims, and has acted as legal counsel for the University of Arizona study on restorative justice involving sexual assault cases.

On a personal note, Lisa has two teenaged children, participates in events supporting youth education and sports. Lisa has lived in Tucson for 20 years, and considers Tucson her home.

attorneys.bio:
Burt is an expert in civil trial work, including personal injury, product liability, medical malpractice and multiple party lawsuits. attorneys.name: Hon. Thomas C. Kleinschmidt
attorneys.practice_type: Mediation Lawyers in Phoenix, AZ
attorneys.bio:
Tom Kleinschmidt joined the firm in 2000 after serving as a Maricopa County Superior Court judge and a judge for the Arizona Court of Appeals for more than 20 years. Judge Kleinschmidt started his legal career in 1966 as an associate with a large law firm in Phoenix where he became a partner.

In 1971, Tom Kleinschmidt became an Assistant Federal Public Defender for the District of Arizona. In 1977, he was appointed to the Maricopa County Superior Court where he served for five years, two of which were as the Presiding Civil Judge.

In 1982, he was appointed to the Arizona Court of Appeals for Division One. Judge Kleinschmidt served as the Chief Judge of Division One from 1994 through 1996, and he remained with the Court of Appeals until 2000.

Since joining Schneider & Onofry of counsel in 2000, Judge Kleinschmidt has worked on several complex cases and served as a private mediator, arbitrator, special discovery master, and as an appellate consultant.

attorneys.firm_name: The Law Office of Robert H. Kleinschmidt, P.C.
attorneys.practice_type: Medical Malpractice Lawyers in Scottsdale, AZ
attorneys.bio:
Rob grew up in Naperville, Illinois and earned his Bachelor of Science degree in 1979 from the University of Illinois majoring in psychology. He obtained his Juris Doctorate in 1982 from the John Marshall Law School in Chicago. He moved to Arizona and served as an administrative assistant and clerk to the Honorable Robert C. Broomfield in 1983. He then defended doctors and hospitals for 5 years under the mentorship of Barry MacBan and Duane Olson. In 1989, Rob started representing victims of medical neglect and chaired the malpractice department at Langerman, Begam, Lewis & Marks through 1993. He opened his own practice in Scottsdale in 1994 and has well over 25 years of experience litigating cases of Medical Negligence, Birth Injury, Surgical Error; defective products and other cases of serious injuries caused by the negligence of others.

Rob is a lifetime member of the Multi-Million Dollar Advocates Forum, which recognizes the accomplishments of lawyers who have won million and multi-million dollar verdicts and settlements for their clients. He is AV rated and listed in Martindale-Hubbell’s Bar Register of Preeminent Lawyers. He helped create new law in the State of Arizona and has several reported cases. He authored "The Right to Videotape Depositions," in The Arizona Trial Lawyers Association Advocate (February 2000). He has lectured on numerous occasions on medical malpractice. Rob has a passion for helping disabled children. He served for several years on the Board of Gompers Rehabilitation Center, a rehabilitation center for seriously disabled children and adults, serving as chairman for 2 years.

He is a member of the State Bar of Arizona; the Maricopa County Bar Association; The American Association for Justice, where he is a member of the Birth Trauma Litigation Group, Professional Negligence Group, Traumatic Brain Injury Litigation Group, and the Nursing Home Litigation Group; and he is a sustaining member of the Arizona Trial Lawyers Association/AzAJ.

attorneys.name: John C. Lacy
attorneys.practice_type: Mining Lawyers in Tucson, AZ
attorneys.bio:
JOHN C. LACY is a Shareholder in the Tucson office. His practice emphasizes mining and public land law and includes cases involving acquisition of land from federal and state land management agencies, title matters and associated water rights. Mr. Lacy also devotes a substantial portion of his time in representation of a telecommunications client. Mr. Lacy has represented clients before administrative boards within the Arizona State Land Department, the United States Department of the Interior and all levels of state and federal courts. A substantial portion of Mr. Lacy's practice is devoted to international mineral transactions and he assisted in the revisions to the mining law of the Republic of Bolivia and the English translation of the mining laws and regulations of Mexico. He also currently serves as an Adjunct Professor in both the College of Law and the College of Mines, Department of Mining and Geological Engineering, University of Arizona where he teaches mining and public land law and oil and gas law. He is the author of numerous publications concerning mineral rights and mineral law history. These publications include a portion of the American Law of Mining, 2d, published by the Rocky Mountain Mineral Law Foundation dealing with the management of school trust lands. Mr. Lacy is a past President of the Rocky Mountain Mineral Law Foundation. He graduated from the University of Arizona College of Law in 1967 and was admitted to the Arizona Bar that same year. A veteran of the Vietnam conflict with the rank of Captain, USAR, JAGC, he is also admitted to practice before the United States Court of Military Appeals.

attorneys.name: Richard W. Langerman
attorneys.practice_type: Bad Faith Insurance Lawyers in Phoenix, AZ
attorneys.bio:
I am Richard Langerman, a trial attorney with over 25 years of experience in handling injury and death cases. My practice areas includes:

Serious Personal Injuries

Wrongful Death

Defective Products

Insurance Bad Faith

Construction Accidents

Automobile Accidents

Trucking Accidents

Motorcycle Accidents

Product Liability

If a manufacturer or retailer sells a defective product, the company is liable for any injuries or death caused by the product defect. I have handled product liability cases involving serious injuries and deaths caused by defectively designed motorcycles, tires, bicycles, car jacks and televisions as well as improperly labeled drugs and fireworks.

I have helped write the laws and have argued cases which have defined product liability for all Arizonans. I was amicus curiae (friend of the court) in Dart v. Wiebe Manufacturing, Inc., 147 Ariz. 242 (1985) (defining the elements of proof in a strict product liability case) and Gosewisch v. American Honda Motor Co., 153 Ariz. 400 (1987) (explaining the elements in a product liability failure to warn case); and represented the injured victim in Rossell v. Volkswagen of America, 147 Ariz. 160 (1985) (explaining the elements of proof in a product liability case based on negligence). I also assisted in drafting Arizona Revised Statutes 12-687 which limits a manufacturer's right to hide self-critical analysis and investigation of defective products and was the principal author of Arizona's jury instructions on product liability law. I have also given a number of lectures on products liability law.

Insurance Bad Faith

Insurance companies are required to pay the benefits outlined in their insurance policies. Insurers also owe a duty of good faith to each policy holder. When an insurance company acts in bad faith, it must pay not only what is owed under the contract, the company must also pay for any other damages it has caused including emotional damage suffered by the policyholder.

I have represented policyholders for over 25 years including bad faith cases involving auto insurance, health insurance, homeowners insurance, and life and disability insurance. I appeared as amicus curiae (friend of the court) in the case of Zilisch v. State Farm Mutual Automobile Ins. Co., 196 Ariz. 234 (2000), in which the Arizona Supreme Court explained what is required by the duty of good faith. I was also the principal author of the jury instructions used in all bad faith cases in Arizona and have lectured extensively on the law of bad faith and the intricacies of trying a bad faith case.

Construction Defect Cases

I have represented a number of workers who were injured by dangerous conditions on their job. I represented the injured worker in Lewis v. Riebe, 170 Ariz. 384 (1992) in which the Arizona Supreme Court explained the duty owed by general contractors to provide for work site safety. My construction site trial experience includes a multimillion dollar victory against the United States government on behalf of seven workers injured while constructing the pipeline connecting the Waddell Dam to the Central Arizona Project.

Automobile Accidents

I have represented families affected by injuries and death from traffic accidents including trucking accidents, accidents involving defective motorcycles and unreasonably dangerous highways. I have lectured on the subjects of using experts in complex automobile litigation and litigation involving highway design defects. My experience includes a $1.8 million verdict on behalf of a young woman injured as a result of defective highway.

attorneys.name: Larry D. Langley
attorneys.practice_type: Civil Litigation and Insurance Defense Lawyers in Scottsdale, AZ
attorneys.bio:
Mr. Langley has been a coverage attorney and insurance defense litigator since 1973, having attained his Juris Doctorate degree from the University of San Francisco Law School. He is actively licensed in Arizona and California and has tried in excess of eighty jury trials in federal and state courts including several first party bad faith, serious injury, wrongful death, professional liability, trademark infringement and punitive damages cases. His most recent defense jury trials in Arizona involved a tire tread separation rollover of a Ford Explorer which resulted in a successful unanimous defense verdict and a defamation, false light and breach of contract action against a Property Owner's Association and Board of Directors. Mr. Langley recently obtained a defense verdict in an insurance bad faith action in California which he co-tried with his partner, Kathleen Langley. He has diversified expertise in construction defect, property, fraud, arson and coverage matters including examinations under oath and appraisals. He is also a licensed civil engineer in the State of California.

Mr. Langley is a member of the American Board of Trial Advocates, American Bar Association, Arizona and California Bar Associations, Defense Research Institute, Northern California Association of Defense Counsel, Arizona Association of Defense Counsel, and the Maricopa County and Scottsdale Bar Associations. He has presented at various continuing education courses and seminars including the ABA and the Property Loss Research Bureau. In 2004 he was featured in Law Technology News regarding his successful defense of a brain injury jury trial in Santa Monica, California.

attorneys.practice_type: Medical Malpractice for Misdiagnosis/Late Diagnosis of Skin Cancer patients - Plaintiffs Lawyers in Scottsdale, AZ
attorneys.bio:
Ms. Langley is the managing partner for the firm and has been a litigator since 1982. She has handled several California and Arizona state court jury trials to verdict involving wrongful death, catastrophic personal injury and dental malpractice claims, has co-tried several jury trials in Arizona with her partner and has handled hundreds of binding and non-binding ADR proceedings, including arbitrations and mediations. She handles a variety of cases, including personal injury, wrongful death and medical malpractice matters, particularly in the area of misdiagnosis and failure to diagnose melanoma. As managing partner, she supervises and mentors the firm's associate attorneys, paralegal and legal assistants and is responsible for teaching them trial practice skills. She has coached the firm's former and present associate attorneys in several Arizona jury trials to verdict.

Ms. Langley received her Juris Doctorate degree from San Francisco Law School in 1981 and is actively licensed in the States of Arizona and California. She is a member of the Arizona and California Bar Associations, American Board of Trial Advocates, Defense Research Institute, Maricopa County and Scottsdale Bar Associations and the Arizona Association of Defense Counsel. She is a trained mediator and co-taught mediation and negotiation courses at Stanford and Hastings Law Schools. She was a faculty member of the 2009 Arizona College of Trial Advocacy. Ms. Langley also has been a member of the Board of Directors for a Scottsdale community association and is currently on the Board of Directors for a charitable non-profit corporation dedicated to cancer research. In addition, she is a volunteer for HopeKids, a non-profit corporation dedicated to children with life-threatening medical conditions.

How do I choose a lawyer?
Comfort Level – Are you comfortable telling the lawyer personal information? Does the lawyer seem interested in solving your problem?
Credentials – How long has the lawyer been in practice? Has the lawyer worked on other cases similar to yours?
Cost – How are the lawyer's fees structured — hourly or flat fee? Can the lawyer estimate the cost of your case?
City – Is the lawyer's office conveniently located?
Not sure what questions to ask a lawyer?
Here are a few to get you started:
How long have you been in practice?
How many cases like mine have you handled?
How often do you settle cases out of court?
What are your fees and costs?

It is always a good idea to research your lawyer prior to hiring. Every state has a disciplinary organization that monitors attorneys, their licenses, and consumer complaints. By researching lawyer discipline you can:
Ensure the attorney is currently licensed to practice in your state
Gain an understanding of his or her historical disciplinary record, if any.
Determine the seriousness of complaints/issues which could range from late bar fees to more serious issues requiring disciplinary action.

attorneys.name: John P. Leader Esq.
attorneys.practice_type: Wrongful Death Lawyers in Tucson, AZ
attorneys.bio:
John has an unmatched legal profile. A graduate (with distinction) from the University of Arizona in 1985, John went on to attend the University of Arizona law school where he received his Juris Doctorate in 1988. During law school, John was a member of the Arizona Law Review. During law school, John had the honor of spending a semester in Washington, D.C., working on "the Hill" for then Senator Dennis DeConcini. After law school, John landed a prestigious federal judicial court clerkship for Judge Alfredo C. Marquez.

In 1990, John was then selected as an Assistant United States Attorney for the U.S. Attorney's Office, where he spent nine years representing the United States of America in the Criminal Division. John received a Special Achievement Award for Sustained Superior Performance of Duty from the U.S. Department of Justice in 1992. As a federal prosecutor, John litigated approximately fifty federal jury trials in the U.S. District Court and presented over 15 oral arguments before the Ninth Circuit Court of Appeals in San Francisco. John has also authored approximately forty Ninth Circuit Court Appellate briefs.

In 1999, John entered private civil practice with the firm of Haralson, Miller, Pitt, and McAnally, where he was an associate to Dale Haralson for three years. During this time, John authored two "Amicus Curiae" Briefs, one that was filed with the U.S. Supreme Court [Norfolk Southern R. Co. v. Shanklin, 529 U.S. 344 (2000)] and another filed with the Arizona Supreme Court [Isbell v. State, 198 Ariz. 291 (2000)].

John opened his legal practice in 2007 and continued private civil litigation on behalf of his clients at the Leader Law Firm. John is a member of the American Trial Lawyer's Association, the Arizona Trial Lawyer's Association, and the Western Trial Lawyer's Association.

In February 2012, John obtained a $7.8 million dollar wrongful death jury verdict against the State of Arizona. In December 2015, John received a $47 million dollar wrongful death jury verdict against the State of Arizona in an I-10 accident case. Read more about these verdicts here: http://www.leaderlawaz.com/roadway-barriers-and-crossover-accidents/.

John Leader is a respected and experienced Catastrophic Personal Injury & Wrongful Death attorney who specializes in helping clients receive justice and compensation for their injuries and losses from negligence or other wrongdoing. We offer a free case evaluation; please contact us today.

attorneys.name: Tim LeDuc
attorneys.practice_type: Personal Injury Lawyers in Phoenix, AZ
attorneys.bio:
Tim LeDuc is an Associate Attorney in the Personal Injury Department at Phillips Law Group. Tim was born and raised here in Arizona where he attended Arizona State University and majored in English Literature. After obtaining his Bachelor’s Degree Tim moved to Malibu, California and obtained his Juris Doctorate Degree from Pepperdine University. While in law school Tim interned at a Personal Injury Firm, a Corporate Litigation Firm, and spent a semester volunteering at a Legal Aid Clinic that specializes in helping those experiencing homelessness in the LA Area with their legal needs. After law school Tim moved back home to his native Arizona and immediately went to work at a Personal Injury Firm here in Phoenix. Tim joined Phillips Law Group shortly after becoming licensed to practice law in the state of Arizona.

Tim is passionate about helping those who have been injured by other’s negligence and ensuring they are treating fairly by large corporations who normally seek to take advantage of them.

When Tim is not working he enjoys watching sports, reading, and spending time with friends.

Tim’s “Why”

I decided to become an attorney because I wanted to help people who were being taken advantage of by large corporations. I felt like the only people who could afford good representation were rich people and I wanted to be an effective advocate for people who could normally not afford quality representation and plaintiff’s work gave me the chance to do that.

attorneys.name: Melissa Lin
attorneys.practice_type: General Liability Lawyers in Phoenix, AZ
attorneys.bio:
Melissa Lin is a partner at Righi Law Group and has earned the AV® Preeminent TM* Peer Review Rating. Her practice includes the representation of individuals, contractors, businesses, and municipalities in tort and

contract litigation, primarily in the areas of general liability, construction defect litigation, complex litigation, personal injury, and product liability. She was honored as a 2012 through 2015 Southwest Super Lawyers Rising Star. She was named to Lawyers of Color's 2013 Inaugural Hot List for the Western Region, and was also named as one of the top valley attorneys by North Valley magazine in 2013.

Melissa prides herself on the early evaluation of cases for creative and early case settlement and resolution. She has successfully defended, mediated, and settled numerous construction defect cases for general contractors and developers involving multiple homeowners and homeowners' associations. She successfully prevailed on a defense motion for summary judgment on a breach of implied warranty claim through appeal, motion for reconsideration, and motion for new trial where Plaintiff alleged damages over a million dollars. The ruling on motion for partial summary judgment limited Plaintiff's damages to approximately $50,000, and led the parties to ultimately settle.

Melissa was second chair for the defense of a multi‐week seven day construction defect trial where Plaintiff was requesting just under a million dollars in damages, and the defense asserted a cost of repair of just under $200,000. The jury found for the defense on common law fraud, consumer fraud, and negligent misrepresentation claims, and only awarded Plaintiff damages on warranty claims in the amount of $230,000.

As a result of defense work on fee‐shifting, Plaintiff agreed to walk away from the trial judgment with each party bearing their own fees and costs.

She was a 2008‐2012 board member of the Women's Metropolitan Arts Council (WoMAC) of the Phoenix Art Museum. She previously served as the 2010‐2011 president, 2009‐2010 vice president of membership and

the 2008‐2009 secretary for WoMAC. She was honored as the December 2011 Volunteer of the Month by the Phoenix Art Museum.

Melissa is the daughter of Taiwanese immigrants. She grew up in Tucson, Arizona where her parents have owned and operated a small business for over thirty‐six years. She enjoys rock climbing, yoga, sprint triathlons,

walking her three dogs, and spending time with her husband.

Michael Lincoln has been licensed to practice law since 2005. He has earned a reputation for being a highly skilled litigator in and out of the courtroom, and has been recognized for his excellence by prominent legal organizations throughout the course of his career. Michael grew up in a military family and lived throughout the country as well as overseas before eventually settling in Arizona. sections.content:
Thomas E. Lordan practices primarily in the areas of commercial and real estate litigation and transactions. He has practiced law for over twenty-five years, both with law firms and in-house, in Ohio, Arizona, Maryland and Washington, D.C. He is admitted to practice in Arizona, Ohio, Maryland, and the District of Columbia.

Mr. Lordan is a graduate of the University of Notre Dame, receiving his Bachelor of Arts Degree with a major in Philosophy in 1971. He graduated from the University of Notre Dame Law School in 1974. He was a member of the Notre Dame London Center for legal studies in London, England during the 1972-1973 academic year.

In 1996, Mr. Lordan received a Master of Arts degree in Political Philosophy from the Catholic University of America in Washington, D.C., and is a candidate for the Ph.D. degree in that field, having completed all but his dissertation.

Mr. Lordan is currently one of three Senior Associates at Wilenchik & Bartness. In that role, he is responsible for supervising and mentoring two junior associates and directing their activities and reviewing their work product.

attorneys.name: Kurt D. Maahs
attorneys.practice_type: Personal Injury Lawyers in Phoenix, AZ
attorneys.bio:
Mr. Maahs joined David Shapiro Law, PLLC in November 2021. For over 25 years, Mr. Maahs has successfully tried, arbitrated, and mediated hundreds of cases ranging from product and automobile liability to commercial litigation.

He's obtained numerous verdicts and settlements worth millions of dollars, including helping a client obtain a $5.7 million settlement for a major trucking accident.

Prior to joining the firm, Mr. Maahs was a managing attorney of the Arizona office of Sweet James, LLP and an assistant managing attorney at Phillips Law Group, P.C., representing victims of personal injury as well as individuals in bad faith actions against insurance companies.

He also spent time as legal counsel for major corporations, including Walgreens, State Farm, Johnson and Johnson, Marriott, and Home Depot.

After earning a degree in criminal justice from the University of Nebraska-Lincoln (1991), he graduated from the University of

Nebraska Law School (1994). Since then, Mr. Maahs has focused on providing the highest quality and most effective representation to his clients. He is admitted to the Bar in the state of Arizona as well as Missouri, Kansas, Nebraska, and Iowa.

When he's not working, Mr. Maahs enjoys spending time with his family, hiking, running, reading, golfing, and following the Nebraska Cornhuskers

attorneys.bio:
